abstract: Plasma electrolytic oxidation (PEO) is a relatively novel method of obtaining thick and durable ceramic coatings on top of valve metals, such as aluminum and its alloys. A combination of electrochemical and thermochemical processes during PEO enables the incorporation of species present in the electrolyte inside the coating. In this systematic study, 6061 aluminum alloy was subjected to plasma electrolytic oxidation in solutions containing yttria-stabilized zirconia (ZrO 2 ), anatase (TiO 2 ), corundum (α-Al 2 O 3 ), and amorphous silica (SiO 2 ) under soft sparking regime (SSR). The electrolytes were modified by adding solid particle suspensions at concentrations of 3, 7, and 10 g L −1 . The aim was to enhance both corrosion resistance and mechanical strength. The resulting coatings were examined for surface morphology, phase composition, microhardness, tribological performance, and corrosion resistance. The results confirmed that particles can be incorporated into the coating during SSR, giving rise to distinct surface morphologies, higher hardness (from 862 ± 220 HV 0.05 for the base electrolyte to 1305 ± 298 HV 0.05 for the 3 g L −1 ZrO 2 variant), lower wear rate (from 70.97 ± 1.33 µm for the base electrolyte to 36.07 ± 0.82 µm for the 3 g L −1 TiO 2 variant at a load of 10 N), and improved corrosion resistance (charge-transfer resistances measured for the 10 g L −1 Al 2 O 3 bath increased by an order of magnitude compared to the Blank sample). The best outcomes were observed at the lowest particles loading (3 g L −1 ) for the SiO 2 - and ZrO 2 -enriched coatings. Higher concentrations were found to be optimal for the electrolytes containing Al 2 O 3 (10 g L −1 ) and TiO 2 (7 g/L −1 ).

title: AI-guided optimization of nanocomposite-based phytoremediation for enhanced soil and crop health in contaminated land
abstract: Contamination of soil by multiple toxic metals requires remediation strategies that combine high removal efficiency, ecological compatibility, and rational materials optimization. Here, an explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-assisted framework was developed to optimize multifunctional GO-biochar-PEI-metal oxide hybrid nanocomposites for coupled contaminant removal and phytoremediation. Random forest (RF) and artificial neural network (ANN) models were trained using independent physicochemical and operational descriptors to predict an Overall Performance Index integrating metal removal, plant biomass, and rhizosphere microbial response. RF outperformed ANN in the held-out test set ( \(\:{R}^{2}=0.9132\) vs. 0.5765) and five-fold cross-validation ( \(\:{R}^{2}=0.585\pm\:0.066\) vs. \(\:0.198\pm\:0.054\) ), demonstrating greater predictive robustness within the investigated design domain. Feature-attribution analysis identified nanocomposite dosage as the dominant design variable without assigning causal significance to model associations. Uncertainty propagation identified a model-predicted high-performance region near 350 mg kg − 1 . At this dosage, the GO-biochar-PEI-CuO hybrid achieved Pb(II), Cr(VI), and U(VI) removal efficiencies of 92.5%, 88.3%, and 85.7%, respectively, outperforming the corresponding TiO₂-containing hybrid. The enhanced performance is consistent with cooperative adsorption, coordination, porous retention, and photothermal-assisted interfacial processes, whereas possible redox transformations remain mechanistic hypotheses requiring direct speciation evidence. Given the simulation-assisted component of the dataset, broader generalizability requires independent experimental validation. Overall, this study establishes an interpretable AI-assisted materials-screening strategy for identifying robust operating windows and guiding the sustainable design of multifunctional hybrid nanocomposites for contaminated-soil remediation.

title: A multifunctional optoelectronic synaptic device for logic operation and neuromorphic computing
abstract: The evolution of energy-efficient neuromorphic hardware capable of mimicking biological synaptic functions is critical for next-generation artificial intelligence and edge-computing systems. However, the integration of optoelectronic synaptic functionality with chemically doped two-dimensional (2D) tungsten diselenide (WSe 2 ) remains insufficiently explored. Here, we report an optically driven neuromorphic memristor based on a tri-layer WSe 2 with engineered carrier polarity via benzyl viologen (BV) doping. The structural integrity and material quality were verified using atomic force microscopy (AFM) and Raman spectroscopy, while electrical characteristics are systematically analyzed using gate-dependent transfer curves ( I ds -V g ) and current-voltage measurements ( I ds -V ds ), supported by an energy band diagram illustrating the Fermi level shift after doping. The BV-doped WSe 2 devices demonstrate pronounced photoresponses under visible and deep-ultraviolet (DUV) illumination, with DUV-induced charge trapping enabling stable memory retention. Optical-pulse stimulation produces tunable conductance modulation, including paired-pulse facilitation (PPF) indicative of short-term plasticity, as well as long-term potentiation and depression. By controlling the DUV pulse duration, the BV-doped WSe 2 device response is increased from 25.2% to 1438.7%. The device further enables selective alphabet recognition and logic OR gate operation. Importantly, synaptic weight characteristics are implemented in an artificial neural network trained to identify handwritten digits on the MNIST dataset with an accuracy of 92%, validated through epoch-dependent learning and confusion matrix analysis. This work may provide a promising platform for low-power, optically programmable neuromorphic systems for intelligent sensing technologies.

title: A multifunctional graphene-integrated double-network nanocomposite hydrogel for dual strain-temperature wearable sensing
abstract: Abstract Inspired by the natural sensing capabilities of human skin, flexible and stretchable materials such as hydrogels have emerged as vital platforms for skin-interfaced and wearable electronics. A double-network chitosan/modified polyethylene glycol/graphene (Cs./mPEG/G) nanocomposite hydrogel is developed as a flexible, multifunctional platform for dual strain-temperature sensing. By leveraging the balanced mechanical properties of the double-network hydrogel and the exceptional electrical conductivity of graphene, the nanocomposite hydrogel possesses strong mechanical resilience and reliable electrical conductivity at strains up to 350%. The sensor effectively tracks various body movements with a gauge factor of 13.8 and maintains cyclic electromechanical stability for over 500 stretching cycles. Additionally, the chitosan-based polymer network exhibits self-adhesion properties due to its terminal hydroxyl and amino groups, which facilitate hydrogen bonding with surfaces such as plastic, rubber, glass, metal, and human tissues. Most importantly, the hydrogel sensor attached to wrists, fingers, elbows, or ankles delivers stable ΔR/R₀ dynamic pulses during movement and detects fever-range temperature changes within 37.5–40 °C in real time, with a linear thermoresistive response and an ultrahigh temperature coefficient of resistance of -5.62% °C⁻¹. These results highlight the potential of the hydrogel nanocomposite as a high-performance dual strain-temperature tactile sensor for wearable healthcare devices and flexible electronics.

title: Monolithically integrated NiCo2Se4 nanowire–carbon cloth cathode scaffolds for non-planar lithium-sulfur structural-battery integration
abstract: Abstract Lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries are attractive for lightweight structural energy-storage systems because of their high theoretical energy density, but their integration into non-planar components is hindered by sulfur-cathode cracking, interfacial delamination, and contact loss under retained curvature and external loading. Here, we report a monolithically integrated NiCo₂Se₄ nanowire/carbon-cloth cathode scaffold (NCSe@CC) for curvature-retained Li–S pouch-cell integration. Direct growth and selenization of Ni–Co precursor nanowires on woven carbon cloth produce a binder-free, interconnected polar host that combines polysulfide-affinitive NiCo₂Se₄ surfaces with continuous electron-transport pathways along the carbon-fiber network. Compared with sulfur-loaded carbon cloth and precursor-coated carbon cloth, S/NCSe@CC exhibits enhanced polysulfide adsorption, reduced charge-transfer resistance, accelerated sulfur-redox kinetics, and improved electrochemical performance, delivering 1,544 mAh g − 1 at 0.1 C with a polarization of 0.13 V. The cathode scaffold retains nanowire–fiber integration after 1,000 curvature-conditioning cycles at a radius of 2.5 mm, and pouch cells assembled with conditioned electrodes show discharge behavior comparable to pristine cells. Under cylindrical curvature, the pouch cell retains 94.0% of its flat-state capacity. Integration into cylindrical, oval, square, and drone-leg geometries further verifies electrical operability after geometric insertion and fixation. This work presents a materials-to-architecture strategy for interface-stable Li–S cathode scaffolds in non-planar structural energy-storage components.

title: Liquid metal‒pectin polysaccharide nanoparticles integrated hydrogel epidermal electrodes for enhanced electrophysiological signal acquisition
abstract: Hydrogel‒based wearable sensors have shown immense potential for real‒time healthcare monitoring due to their tissue-like softness and biocompatibility. However, ensuring smooth signal transmission along with stable, long‒lasting, and comfortable adhesion at the skin–electrode interface by using hydrogels remains challenging due to their dehydration, mechanical fragility, and inconsistent adhesion to skin. Achieving high quality signal acquisition is especially critical in the lower frequency range of the electrophysiological bandwidth (0.1–100 Hz) due to the signal quality deteriorated by high skin–electrode impedance, motion artifacts, and external noise. Herein, we fabricated pectin‒encapsulated liquid metal (LM) nanoparticles‒incorporated conductive hydrogel (PeLM‒CH)‒based epidermal electrode that can improve the signal‒to‒noise ratio (SNR) of electrocardiogram (ECG) and electromyogram (EMG) signals while ensuring a stable and conformable skin–electrode interface. The PeLM‒CH was synthesized via the incorporation of pectin‒encapsulated LM particles into a hydrogel matrix, followed by doping with an ionically conductive salt solution. The fabricated PeLM‒CH epidermal electrode possesses both metallic conductivity of LM and ionic conductivity of doped hydrogel, thereby demonstrating an appreciable decrease in skin–electrode impedance and high quality signal transmission from the human body enabled by enhanced the SNR of ECG (SNR, 15.05 dB) and EMG (SNR, 20.98 dB). This study introduces a PeLM‒CH‒based epidermal electrode that effectively addresses the limitations of conventional gel electrodes in epidermal electrophysiological monitoring applications. The outcome of this work highlights the improved functionality of PeLM‒CH gel electrodes in clean, high‒precision electrophysiological monitoring, attributed to their excellent skin conformity and relatively low interfacial impedance in the electrophysiological bandwidth.

title: Multifunctional meta-absorber for multispectral camouflage against infrared, radar, and microwave radiometric detection
abstract: The rapid advancement of integrated detection systems poses a severe threat to the survivability of high-value ground targets. However, conventional camouflage strategies typically focus on individual detection methods. As microwave radiometers are increasingly integrated into modern detection systems, existing strategies exhibit limitations in addressing the challenges posed by multispectral detection systems. Herein, a multifunctional meta-absorber is proposed, numerically and experimentally demonstrating integrated multispectral camouflage capabilities against infrared, radar, and microwave radiometric detection. The meta-absorber consists of an infrared shielding layer (IRSL) and a radar absorption-microwave emissivity layer (RAMEL). The IRSL is realized through a frequency-selective surface, achieving a low infrared emissivity of 0.334 while ensuring efficient microwave transmission. The RAMEL utilizes a multilayer stacked structure and is based on the ohmic loss mechanism, achieving over 90% broadband absorption in the 4.62–28.29 GHz. This absorption performance leads to a substantial reduction in the radar cross section, achieving a 10 dB reduction in the 4.38–21.18 GHz. More importantly, based on Kirchhoff’s law of thermal radiation, the meta-absorber employs its high microwave emissivity to minimize the brightness temperature contrast between metallic targets and the background, resulting in a 40.33% reduction in the average contrast. Characterized by low infrared emissivity, high absorptivity, high microwave emissivity, wide-angle stability, and polarization insensitivity, the proposed meta-absorber provides a viable solution for multispectral camouflage, enhancing the survivability of high-value ground targets.

title: Substrate-activated autocatalytic in-situ fabrication of nano-structured titanium oxide/carbon hybrid gradient modified layers on titanium bipolar plates for proton exchange membrane fuel cells
abstract: Metallic bipolar plates (BPs) are critical components of proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), yet poor corrosion resistance and high interfacial contact resistance (ICR) hinder their commercialization. Conventional ex-situ coating methodologies suffer from instability, non-uniform coverage, complex preparation process and high cost. To overcome these challenges, a novel and facile substrate-activated autocatalytic in-situ growth strategy combining chemical etching, electroless plating, and heat treatment is proposed to fabricate a nano-structured titanium oxide/carbon hybrid gradient modified layer (NTOC) on Ti substrates. The NTOC with thickness 200 nm features a tripartite architecture comprising an amorphous carbon outer layer, an intermediate zone dominated by oxygen-vacancy-containing titanium oxide, and a Ti-O-C transition layer. This unique architecture enables atomic-level carbon/titanium oxide integration and strong interfacial metallurgical bonds, which shows high corrosion resistance (< 1 µA cm − 2 ) and quite low ICR (1.05 mΩ cm 2 ), far surpassing the Department of Energy 2025 targets for BPs. Moreover, NTOC modified Ti BPs in PEMFCs yield a peak power density up to 1200.6 mW cm − 2 , exceeding that of untreated Ti BPs by almost twofold (664.19 mW cm − 2 ) and the current study (1160.1 mW cm − 2 ). Therefore, this study offers a transformative solution for enhancing performance of BPs, accelerating the commercialization of PEMFCs.

title: Interfacial charge engineering of Pt-Mo2C heterostructures for robust oxygen reduction reaction
abstract: Abstract The commercialization of fuel cells is severely impeded by the sluggish kinetics of oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) and instability of conventional Pt/C catalysts, primarily due to weak metal-support interactions. Here, we propose an interfacial charge engineering strategy to construct robust Pt-Mo 2 C heterostructures on nitrogen-doped carbon. Synthesized via a scalable, in-situ concurrent pyrolysis-reduction, the nanocomposite features precisely modulated electronic coupling. X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy confirms strong interfacial interaction, delineated by a distinct Pt-Mo bond (~ 2.72 Å) and a high Pt-Mo coordination number (~ 1.81). Theoretical calculations demonstrate that this heterostructured interface functions as an electronic reservoir, driving directional charge redistribution. This transfer downshifts the d -band center of interfacial Pt atoms, thereby optimizing the binding strength of oxygenated intermediates and accelerating ORR kinetics. Electrocatalytic measurements reveal that the engineered Pt-Mo 2 C/NC catalyst delivers an outstanding mass activity of 0.65 A mg − 1 Pt at 0.9 V, outperforming commercial Pt/C by a factor of 4.8. Moreover, the robust Pt-Mo 2 C coupling effectively suppresses Pt dissolution and agglomeration, endowing the catalyst with exceptional durability, retaining ~ 90% of its mass activity after 20,000 potential cycles. These results offer a general design principle for active, durable electrocatalysts based on targeted interfacial electronic modulation.

title: Correction: An injectable multi-functional strontium based gentiopicroside hydrogel accelerates bone regeneration via immunomodulation and promoting osteo-/angiogenesis effects
abstract: During a routine post-publication re-examination the authors identified several figure-assembly errors in which the same micrograph had inadvertently been placed into two different treatment groups.The following issues should be corrected:1. Figure 4H (CD31 immunofluorescence of HUVECs): The Sr and GPS columns in the CD31/DAPI/Merge rows were assembled from the same raw image.

title: Protein-rich fibrous eggshell membrane derived ZnO 3D-nanohybrid for cryoprotectant, reproductive scavengers against Zn deficiency and hypokalemic effects in rats
abstract: Zinc deficiency is associated with impaired spermatogenesis, reduced sperm quality, and male infertility, highlighting the need for multifunctional biomaterials capable of supporting sperm preservation and reproductive health. Herein, we report, for the first time, the synthesis of protein-rich eggshell membrane (ESM)-supported ZnO nanocomposites with distinct ZnO nanostructures uniformly anchored onto a three-dimensional fibrous ESM scaffold. The hypothesis of this study was that ESM-supported ZnO nanocomposites could provide controlled Zn²⁺ release, antimicrobial protection, and enhanced sperm preservation while simultaneously improving reproductive and metabolic health in vivo. To evaluate this hypothesis, two experimental phases were conducted. First, the antimicrobial activity and sperm cryoprotective performance of ESM-ZnO nanocomposites were investigated under heat-shock and freeze–thaw conditions. Antibacterial and antifungal activities were assessed alongside sperm viability, reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, DNA integrity, motility, and morphological characteristics. Subsequently, the biological efficacy of the optimized formulation was validated in male Sprague-Dawley rats through reproductive, biochemical, and histological analyses. The results demonstrated that the thermally synthesized ESM-ZnO-T nanocomposite exhibited superior physicochemical characteristics, improved colloidal stability, sustained Zn²⁺ release behavior, and enhanced antimicrobial efficacy. ESM-ZnO-T effectively preserved sperm viability, morphology, motility, and DNA integrity, achieving an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.84 following cryopreservation. In vivo investigations further revealed improved reproductive hormone profiles, spermatogenesis, sperm morphology, and testicular histology compared with control groups. Moreover, ESM-ZnO-T contributed to the regulation of hypokalemia and hyperoxaluria-associated biochemical alterations while supporting normal liver and kidney function. Overall, the developed ESM-ZnO-T nanocomposite represents a promising multifunctional biomaterial platform for antimicrobial protection, sperm cryopreservation, and reproductive health management, providing a potential strategy for addressing zinc deficiency-associated male infertility.

title: Bio-inspired temperature-responsive hydrogels for antibacterial oral protection and dental whitening with significant pyroelectric dynamic efficacy
abstract: Dental whitening, as one of the most popular procedures in aesthetic dentistry, has attracted significant attention from both clinicians and researchers. Herein, a bio-inspired wet-adhesive CD/TA 2 /SF/BM (CDT 2 FB) hydrogel was fabricated for dental whitening and broad-spectrum antibacterial protection. Silk fibroin (SF), L-3,4-dihydroxyphenylalanine (DOPA)-grafted chitosan (CD) and tannic acid (TA) were incorporated to mimic the adhesive mechanisms of barnacles and mussels. Under repeated cooling/heating cycles, BM heterojunction within the hydrogel exhibited an efficient intrinsic pyroelectric effect, facilitated the separation of electron-hole pairs, constructed a built-in microelectric field, and ultimately promoted the in-situ generation of •OH and •O 2 − radicals. Natural black stains on the dentition surface were successfully whitened in CDT 2 FB + ΔT group, achieving 8.1-fold enhancement in whiteness (color difference/ΔE: 26.6 ± 3.0). Notably, the group of CDT 2 FB + ΔT exhibited a strongest bactericidal activity, achieving a remarkable elimination rate of 93.8 ± 0.6% against E. coli and 89.8 ± 1.2% against S. aureus , respectively. Simultaneously, the hydrogel acted as a protective patch that isolated the dental surface from the acidic environment and inhibited glucose accumulation. Hence, the hydrogel was capable of maintaining enamel health and lowering cariogenic risk, delivering dual therapeutic and protective effects, and thus showed great potential for practical dental applications.

title: Correction: Bio-inspired interface-structure synergy unlocking synchronized helicoidal toughening in stiffness-mismatched hybrid materials
Mineral-SiO2 composites: synthesis methods and functional applications
abstract: Mineral-SiO 2 composites represent a versatile category of functional materials, combining natural abundance, structural variability, and cost-effectiveness of minerals with the adjustable physicochemical characteristics of SiO 2 . This review offers a comprehensive and up-to-date overview of the fabrication approaches used to prepare mineral-SiO 2 composites. Various fabrication methods, such as mechano-chemical, chemical precipitation, sol–gel, microemulsion method, are systematically discussed in terms of their mechanisms, advantages, and limitations in controlling structure and interface. The resulting composites exhibit broad applicability across environmental remediation, heterogeneous catalysis, pigments, functional fillers, ceramic opacifiers, and advanced coatings such as superhydrophobic surfaces. Finally, current challenges, including relatively high cost of some of the preparation methods, limited scalability and reproducibility and narrow applicability are critically analyzed, and future perspectives are proposed accordingly, highlighting the importance of well-designed products preparation and specific application. This review aims to provide fundamental insights and strategic guidance for the rational development of next-generation mineral-SiO 2 composites.

title: Enhanced dielectric performance of polypropylene for hvdc cable insulation via 4‑allyloxybenzil grafting for multiscale structural modulation
abstract: Impact Polypropylene Copolymer (IPC) is a promising candidate for HVDC cable insulation, yet the lack of rigorous, quantitative structure-property correlations limits its performance optimization. In this study, a functional monomer, 4-Allyloxybenzil (AOB), containing benzene rings, carbonyl groups, and ether bonds, was synthesized and grafted onto IPC via an aqueous suspension method to enhance its dielectric properties. Distinct from traditional cross-scale analyses, this work establishes direct quantitative correlations within specific scales before integrating them into a comprehensive model. At the micro-scale, Density Functional Theory (DFT) and Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy (KPFM) revealed that the specific molecular structure of AOB introduces deep electron (HOMO) and hole (LUMO) traps. This modification significantly prolonged the surface potential decay time from 3.9 s to 9.2 s, effectively suppressing carrier injection and mobility. At the meso-scale, AOB acted as a nucleating agent, refining spherulites and increasing crystalline density. Finite element simulations based on the Voronoi algorithm demonstrated that this morphological evolution reduced the dielectric mismatch between crystalline and amorphous phases, thereby decreasing the interfacial electric field distortion from 43% to 21%. Consequently, at the macro-scale, the synergistic effect of micro-scale trap capture and meso-scale field homogenization resulted in an 85% reduction in space charge accumulation, a one-order-of-magnitude decrease in conductivity, and a 30% increase in DC breakdown strength. This study provides a multi-scale, quantitative theoretical basis for the rational design of advanced cable insulation materials.

title: Kinetically moderated reprotonation reconstructs aramid nanofiber hydrogen-bond networks for high-performance thermal management and EMI shielding composite films
abstract: Flexible electronic devices urgently require lightweight multifunctional films that can dissipate heat, suppress electromagnetic interference (EMI), and retain mechanical reliability under repeated deformation. However, filler-rich polymer composites often improve thermal/electrical transport at the expense of matrix integrity, creating a persistent trade-off between thermal conductivity and mechanical robustness. Herein, we report a kinetically moderated reprotonation strategy that shifts the design principle from filler-dominated transport enhancement to time-scale-controlled reconstruction of the aramid nanofiber (ANF) matrix. The acetic acid/ethanol (AE) route couples moderate acid-assisted amide proton recovery with subsequent solvent exchange and nanofiber rearrangement before complete network consolidation. This controlled sequence enables progressive restoration of hydrogen bonding (N–H···O = C) and formation of a dense, ordered ANF-AE nanofibrillar framework. Consequently, the pure ANF-AE film achieves an in-plane thermal conductivity (λ∥) of 7.7 W·m–1·K–1 and a tensile strength of 220 MPa, corresponding to a 133% increase in λ∥ compared with water-reprotonated ANF. After incorporating PDA-functionalized graphene nanoplatelets (fGNP) further strengthens the reconstructed network through hydrogen-bonding and π–π interfacial interactions. The optimized fGNP50/ANF-AE composite film achieves a λ∥ of 81 W·m–1·K–1, EMI shielding effectiveness of 57 dB at 60 μm, tensile strength of 368 MPa, and toughness of 20 MJ‧m− 3. Moreover, the composite retains approximately 95% of its initial properties after 10,000 folding cycles and exhibits excellent thermal stability. This work demonstrates that kinetically moderated ANF reconstruction combined with non-covalent graphene interfacial engineering offers an effective route toward multifunctional composite films for advanced flexible electronics. Kinetically moderated AE reprotonation reconstructed a dense hydrogen-bonded ANF matrix. Pure ANF-AE film achieved λ∥ of 7.7 W·m–1·K–1, as compared to conventional ANF-W. fGNP50/ANF-AE composite film achieved λ∥ of 81 W‧m⁻¹‧K⁻¹ and EMI SET of 57 dB at 60 μm. PDA-mediated fGNP/ANF coupling produced 368 MPa tensile strength and 20 MJ‧m-3 toughness. Hydrogen-bond reconstruction and fGNP interfacial coupling enabled multifunctional flexible films.

title: Fiber-reinforced polymer composite interfaces: research progress on mechanisms, modification, and multifunctionalization
abstract: The performance of fiber-reinforced polymer composites is highly contingent upon the properties of the interfacial region between the fiber and the matrix. The interface acts not only as a critical medium for load transfer but also fundamentally governs the damage evolution mechanisms and the resultant macroscopic performance of the material. With increasing applications of composites in aerospace and advanced equipment, interfacial research has progressed from simply pursuing strong bonding to the deliberate design of interfacial structure and functionality. This paper reviews recent advances in composite interface science. First, the physicochemical mechanisms of interfacial bonding and typical failure modes are analyzed to establish the relationship between interface behavior and macroscopic performance. Second, various interfacial modification strategies, including chemical treatment, physical methods, and coating techniques, are compared in terms of their working mechanisms and limitations. Third, the use of nanoparticles and nanofilms to enhance interlaminar performance is discussed, along with their toughening mechanisms. Finally, the emerging trend of developing the interface from a mechanical link into a multifunctional platform is considered, and current challenges such as scalable fabrication and long-term reliability are summarized. This review aims to provide useful insights for both fundamental research and practical applications of composite interfaces.

title: Gallic acid functionalized Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene/SPES hybrid tight ultrafiltration membranes with improved interfacial stability for wastewater treatment
abstract: The limited oxidation stability and affinity of Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene with polymer restrict its application in polymeric membranes for wastewater treatment. Herein, polyphenol derivative gallic acid (GA) functionalized MXene (gMX) was incorporated into sulfonated poly (ether sulfone) (SPES) to fabricate novel gMX-SPES hybrid tight UF membranes. GA functionalization improved oxidation stability in water, dispersion of functionalized MXene (gMX) and interfacial affinity to SPES. The interfacial interactions influenced membrane morphology, pore-size distribution, average pore size, hydrophilicity, and surface charge characteristics. At an optimal gMX loading of 2 wt%, the corresponding membrane gMX2 achieved pure-water flux (J w ) of 16.4 L m⁻² h⁻¹ bar⁻¹, represents 4.3-fold enhancement over the pristine SPES membrane. In separate single-solute tests, the optimized membrane gMX2 achieved > 95% rejection of selected dyes and pharmaceuticals under synthetic feed conditions, while maintaining improved flux stability and antifouling performance during filtration of pharmaceutical-spiked hospital wastewater. During 24 h crossflow filtration of pharmaceutical-spiked hospital wastewater, the permeate flux (J p ) of gMX2 was lowered to 11 L m⁻² h⁻¹ bar⁻¹, with removal efficiencies of 77% for AMT and 54% for CIP compared to MX2. The findings further support gMX-SPES membranes as a pretreatment option for reducing pharmaceutical loads in hospital wastewater.

title: Quasi-zero stiffness TPU interlayer for aluminium–polymer pipe-in-pipe systems: design, modeling and multifunctional performance
abstract: An architected thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) interlayer is proposed for aluminium pipe-in-pipe (PIP) systems to combine load-bearing capacity with vibration attenuation. The interlayer is designed to exhibit a quasi-zero stiffness (QZS) response through geometric deformation. Analytical models are developed to describe its quasi-static force–displacement response and dynamic displacement transmissibility. Finite element simulations and compression and vibration experiments are used to assess plateau force, plateau width, specific energy absorption (SEA), and vibration transmission. Parametric studies examine the influence of material properties and geometric parameters on these performance measures. The results indicate that parameter variations can increase the QZS plateau width by 200%–300% relative to the baseline configuration and modify the plateau force. Three representative configurations are experimentally evaluated to examine the predicted compression and vibration responses. Differences between numerical predictions and experimental measurements are discussed in relation to material behavior, manufacturing variability, and boundary conditions. The study characterizes the relationship between interlayer geometry, compressive response, and vibration transmission, providing a basis for further development of architected interlayers for tubular assemblies.

title: Bio-inspired flexible pressure sensors: morphology-guided structure–function relationships, reliability, and future perspectives
abstract: Bio-inspired flexible pressure sensors have emerged as a major class of soft sensing systems for wearable electronics, electronic skin, human–machine interfaces, and soft robotics because biological structures provide effective design principles for regulating deformation, contact evolution, and interfacial adaptation. However, the field remains difficult to compare critically because reported performance is often discussed through isolated sensitivity values, while the structural origins of signal generation, the pressure-regime dependence of response, and the reliability limits of the underlying architectures are not examined in a unified manner. This review addresses that gap through a morphology-centered perspective, in which bio-inspired pressure sensors are analyzed according to the engineered structural motifs that govern their function. Surface-relief and contact-engineered architectures, porous and three-dimensional frameworks, interfacial, interlocking, and adhesive systems, and hierarchical or discontinuity-driven designs are examined in relation to their coupling with piezoresistive, capacitive, iontronic, triboelectric, piezoelectric, and hybrid transduction pathways. Across these classes, sensitivity, operating range, dynamic response, hysteresis, drift, durability, and failure behavior are traced to the pressure-responsive structural features that define each architecture. This analysis further shows that features designed to amplify signal often also set the boundaries for reversibility and long-term stability. Finally, current challenges in benchmarking and validation are discussed, with emphasis on the need for morphology-traceable reporting, realistic reliability assessment, and structure-guided design rules for future bio-inspired flexible pressure sensors.

title: Correction: Oxygen-scavenging MnO2 nanoparticles enabled thermally stable and oxidation-resistant MXene inks for 3D-printed flexible asymmetric supercapacitors
Hollow bowl‑like MXene/FeNi3 heterostructures for electromagnetic wave absorption and photo‑thermo‑electric conversion
abstract: Abstract Driven by the rapid advancement of modern electronic and wireless technologies , multifunctional electromagnetic wave absorption (EMA) materials are urgently demanded in radar camouflage, 5G/6G communications and energy utilization. However, traditional EMA absorbers face a critical challenge in reconciling the inherent trade-off between high-efficiency absorption and multifunctional integration. Inspired by bioinspired architecture, we construct an open hollow bowl-like MXene/FeNi 3 heterostructure that enables precise modulation of interfacial charge distribution, thereby triggering synergistic effects among interfacial charge transport, oxygen vacancy defects and magnetic interaction. Benefiting from these merits, the optimized MXene/FeNi 3 achieves extraordinarily EMA performances with a minimum reflection loss (RLₘ i ₙ) of − 61.44 dB, an effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 6.31 GHz at 1.91 mm, and a Radar Cross section value of − 45.36 dB·m 2 . Furthermore, MXene/FeNi 3 exhibits outstanding photo-thermo-electric conversion performance, attaining a steady surface temperature of 56.7 °C upon 1-sun illumination, maintaining photothermal stability for over 6 h under 2-sun irradiation, and achieving an open-circuit voltage of 225.8 mv and a short-circuit current of 38.9 mA under 1-sun illumination. Importantly, this architecture design strategy is readily extendable to other magnetic systems, including Co, CoFe, CoNi, and FeCoNi, establishing a versatile platform for next-generation multifunctional integrated EMA materials.

title: Traffic light intelligent early warning platform for mercury: deep eutectic fluorescent composite with cascade signal enhancement function
abstract: Mercury (Hg) is highly toxic, so its monitoring is vital for environmental and public health. Conventional detection methods depend on bulky equipment with low efficiency, so there is an urgent need for fast, portable, and precise mercury sensing techniques to mitigate the hazards associated with mercury overexposure. Therefore, using deep eutectic solvent (DES) as a regulation medium, this study fabricates a partially rigid, delocalized conjugated fluorescent responsive material with intramolecular coupled positive-negative-junction, and integrates it with computer vision to build a traffic-light-style intelligent early warning platform. Benefiting from the Ⅱ5 6 delocalized conjugated system, the material possesses excellent luminescence performance. This material exhibits excellent selective fluorescence quenching against Hg 2+ . Critically, the inherent dynamic hydrogen-bond network of its internal DES can realize preconcentration of target metal ions. This synergistic “preconcentration-response” mechanism greatly amplifies fluorescent signals, granting the eutectic fluorescent probe outstanding sensitivity with a detection limit of 60 nmol/L toward Hg 2+ . Subsequently, the YOLOv8 algorithm and traffic-light grading logic were incorporated into portable terminal to construct an intelligent early-warning platform. This platform establishes a quantitative mapping relationship between sample color information and actual analyte concentrations. Detection results of multiple samples can be acquired within 472 ms, with overall recoveries ranging from 91.16% to 109.35%. Built-in red/yellow/green indicators mark hazard, alert, and safe tiers for high-throughput visual intelligent analysis. The as-prepared deep eutectic probe composite enables sensitive detection via the intelligent early-warning platform, exhibits great prospects for environmental monitoring. This strategy provides a new approach to point-of-care sensing of toxic contaminants.

title: One-step fabrication of a porous hBN/PDMS composite membrane for breathable and thermally dissipative skin-interface applications
abstract: Abstract Skin-interfaced materials for wearable applications must simultaneously provide effective thermal management, breathability, and mechanical conformability, yet conventional approaches often sacrifice thermal performance for breathability. Here, we report a simple, one-step strategy for the fabrication of a porous hexagonal boron nitride (hBN)/polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) membrane using perfluorohexane (PFH) as a volatile porogen. This approach directly produces a stable porous architecture during casting and curing, eliminating the need for washing, solvent extraction, or post-fabrication treatment. The pore size is tuned based on the curing temperature, which controls the kinetic competition between matrix curing and PFH volatilization. The overall porosity rises from about 15% to 31% with an increase in the PFH content. Importantly, this porous membrane overcomes the conventional trade-off between thermal conductivity and breathability. Although air voids are present, the membrane achieves a thermal conductivity of 0.22 W/m·K, which is comparable to that of the dense form of the composite. This is because the hBN nanoplatelets assemble along the pore walls, forming continuous heat-conduction pathways. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations reveal the more effective transfer of heat near the hBN/PDMS composite interface in the porous membrane, which is consistent with the lower heat accumulation observed experimentally. In vivo analysis demonstrates that the porous membrane maintains skin hydration at a stable level of approximately 103–107% and has a mechanical compliance close to that of bare skin, ensuring both physiological and mechanical comfort. These findings establish the proposed one-step fabrication strategy as a material-level foundation for the design of breathable, thermally functional membranes for future skin-interface applications.

title: Decoupling of factors influencing interface characteristics in basalt fiber-reinforced polymer composites
abstract: Intermolecular interactions, the relative contributions of interfacial factors, and their roles in strengthening fiber-reinforced composites remain insufficiently understood. Here, computational simulations are employed to perform decoupling analysis of chemical groups and surface morphology at basalt fiber(BF)-reinforced composite interfaces and to elucidate the regulatory effect of silane coupling agent on resin conformations. γ-aminopropyl triethoxysilane (KH550) balances highly positive and negative electrostatic regions on the BF surface, promoting multiple binding sites with resin molecules. At the BF/polyamide 66 (PA66) interface, KH550 modification increases the number of hydrogen bonds by 10.4% and makes the interfacial interaction energy more negative, from -384.4 to -487.9 kcal/mol. For BF-PA66, BF-epoxy resin (EP), and BF-polypropylene (PP) composites, interactions provided by KH550’s amino groups contribute more to interface mechanical enhancement than surface morphologies. At the BF/PA66 interface, amino-group introduction and atomic-scale morphology modification enhance the interfacial mechanical response by factors of 1.49 and 1.29, respectively. For BF-PA66 and BF-EP interface, atomic-level surface morphology regulating resin molecular chain arrangement conformations optimizes mechanical properties more effectively than surface asperities enabling resin infiltration. KH550 transforms resin molecular chains from surface-aligned conformations into interpenetrating structures due to enhanced interaction and steric hindrance effects. Atomic nanoindentation reveals that KH550 modification redirects resin deformation from interfacial sliding to bulk-matrix deformation, leading to a transition from adhesive to cohesive failure and increasing the maximum indentation force from approximately 2.9 to 4.0 nN. This research clarifies the intrinsic interfacial strengthening mechanism and provides guidance for rational interphase design.

title: Nanointerface engineering of leach-resistant hybrid graphene oxide-metal oxide-sand composites for sustainable removal of emerging pollutants
abstract: The practical deployment of photocatalytic nanomaterials in water treatment is hindered by catalyst leaching, nanoparticle aggregation, and poor long-term stability. Herein, we report a scalable nanointerface engineering strategy to construct hierarchical nano-micro composites by immobilizing graphene oxide (GO)-metal oxide hybrid coatings onto granular sand through a water-based, binder-assisted layer-by-layer assembly using polyvinyl alcohol as an interfacial linker. GO was hybridized with representative metal oxide photocatalysts (TiO 2 , W-TiO 2 , ZnO, and WO 3 ) to create heterostructured coatings with enhanced adsorption and photocatalytic activity. Comprehensive physicochemical characterization confirmed the uniform deposition and integration of the nanophases on the sand substrate without detectable structural degradation. Using triamterene as a model emerging pharmaceutical contaminant, TiO 2 -GO-sand achieved 87–90% removal under UV and visible-light irradiation while maintaining high performance (~ 100%) over a broad pH (3–8). Under optimized conditions, high removal efficiencies were also achieved for rhodamine B and methylene blue. Kinetic analysis followed pseudo-second-order behavior with apparent rate constants of 0.043–0.057 min − 1 . Radical scavenging tests revealed an adsorption-assisted photocatalytic mechanism dominated by synergistic •OH and •O 2− pathways, with adsorption contributing approximately 57% of the total triamterene removal. No detectable GO or TiO 2 leaching was observed after 12 months of continuous aqueous exposure, and the composite maintained stable performance over 20 regeneration cycles. Validation in hospital wastewater and river water further confirmed robust pollutant removal under realistic conditions. This work establishes a universal nano-micro interface engineering strategy for developing durable, scalable and environmentally-safe photocatalytic composites, advancing the practical implementation of nano-micromaterial-enabled water purification technologies.

title: Silane-mediated organic–inorganic interfacial regulation improves deformation coordination and structural integrity of silica-rich oil well cement under hydrothermal conditions
abstract: Improving deformation coordination at interfacial regions is a potential strategy for maintaining the structural integrity of silica-rich oil well cement under high-temperature hydrothermal conditions. Amino silane (ASMR) was introduced to regulate organic–inorganic interfacial interactions. The macro- and micro-mechanical properties, volumetric deformation, pore structure, product evolution, surface chemical environments, strain distribution, and strength retention during extended hydrothermal curing were investigated. XRD results showed that ASMR did not fundamentally alter the principal hydrothermal product evolution path, while the TG-derived non-evaporable water estimates exhibited similar temperature-dependent evolution in both systems. XPS results indicated ASMR-derived N-containing species on the analyzed hydration-product surfaces and associated changes in the local surface chemical environment, while EDS mapping provided complementary information on the spatial occurrence of ASMR-derived N-containing species within the analyzed microstructural regions. After curing at 150, 180, and 200 °C, the strength of the blank oil well cement decreased from 50.4 MPa to 29.1 MPa, whereas the ASMR-modified system maintained a comparable strength of 29.6 MPa at 200 °C. The ultimate tensile strain increased from 678, 503, and 631 µε for the blank group to 1182, 1414, and 1378 µε for the modified group. Under 200 °C curing, the coefficient of variation of surface strain distribution after 48 h decreased from 1.33 to 0.83, and the strength retrogression rate from 2 to 28 d decreased from 40.1% to 16.6%. These results suggest that ASMR-mediated organic–inorganic interfacial regulation is associated with improved local deformation coordination, reduced expansion-induced strain localization, and mitigated strength retrogression.

title: Carbon-Supply-Programmed CNT Growth for Ultrathin Microwave Absorbers from Waste Batteries and Plastics
abstract: The rapid expansion of 5G/6G communication networks has intensified the demand for lightweight, efficient, and broadband microwave absorbing materials (MAMs) to mitigate electromagnetic pollution. Co-upcycling spent lithium-ion batteries and plastic waste into high-value functional materials represents a sustainable pathway but requires precise control over carbon nanostructure formation. Here, we introduce a carbon-supply-driven kinetic regulation strategy to program carbon nanotube (CNT) growth during the one-step co-pyrolysis of waste nickel cobalt manganese oxide (NCM) cathodes and low-density polyethylene (LDPE). We demonstrate that the NCM/LDPE mass ratio serves as a key parameter to regulate local carbon flux, thereby continuously tuning CNT elongation while inducing a volcano-type evolution of the defect-related Raman intensity ratio (I D /I G ). This non-monotonic behavior reveals an intrinsic competition between graphitization and defect generation, whose optimal balance is crucial for microwave absorption. The optimized sea urchin-like architecture (NCC-6.7) integrates an interconnected conductive network for conduction loss with abundant structural defects and heterogeneous interfaces for dipolar polarization, achieving a remarkable minimum reflection loss of − 63.45 dB at an ultrathin thickness of 1.63 mm and an effective absorption bandwidth of 4.25 GHz at 1.46 mm. Moreover, the NCC-6.7-derived textile exhibits enhanced corrosion resistance, reduced electromagnetic scattering, and excellent mechanical flexibility. This work establishes a kinetics-structure–property paradigm for designing advanced composite absorbers, and the resulting textile demonstrates great potential for flexible electromagnetic protection and marine applications. This work not only provides a practical route for valorizing mixed solid wastes but also offers new opportunities for sustainable electromagnetic pollution mitigation.

title: Chain-length-dependent structure–activity relationships in the deep oxidation of multi-component aldehydes over an S-scheme ternary bismuth oxynitride/titanium dioxide/graphite heterojunction photocatalyst
abstract: Photocatalytic oxidation (PCO) offers a scalable route for indoor aldehyde abatement, yet practical deployment is hindered by potential surface deactivation from competitive adsorption and accumulation of oxygenated intermediates under realistic multi-component and humidified conditions. Here, a series of ternary heterojunctions, comprising bismuth oxynitride (Bi 5 O 7 NO 3 : BN), titanium dioxide (TiO 2 : T), and graphite (G) (denoted as TGBN-x, “x” = BN/TG wt%), are immobilized on honeycomb cordierite and integrated into a portable air purifier (AP) device. In a 23-L closed-loop chamber, these AP-PCO systems are evaluated for abatement of single- and mixed-aldehydes [formaldehyde (FA), acetaldehyde (AA), propionaldehyde (PA), and valeraldehyde (VA)] under varying operating conditions. Under dry conditions, the optimized TGBN-10 filter records 100% FA (5 ppm) removal within 6 min of 1 W UV-LED illumination, while doubling the catalyst loading from 0.05 to 0.1 g enhances the chamber clean air delivery rate (CADR) from 8.3 to 16.0 L min − 1 . It also exhibits superior charge-carrier dynamics (relative to binary and single counterpart catalysts), delivering an 8.93-fold higher specific CADR (SCADR) at 5 ppm FA (near-ambient level) than at 100 ppm (industrially-relevant level), and a 1.70-fold higher SCADR than the binary TG composite under identical conditions. At 100 ppm FA (100 ppm per aldehyde in the mixture), its SCADR increases 2.64-fold (from 7 to 18.51 L min − 1 g − 1 ) when the inlet gas-phase shifts from a multi-component to a single-component system, underscoring the strong dependence of PCO performance on both inlet concentration and gas-phase composition. In a multi-component mixture (total C 0 = 100 ppm), the peak PCO reaches 91% for FA, compared with 23.2% (PA), 60.7% (VA), and 5.8% (AA), while the overall CO 2 yield across all aldehydes attains 95.9%, confirming a deep mineralization pathway. In situ DRIFTS measurements reveal hydroxyl-mediated FA activation via dioxymethylene and formate intermediates, with carboxylate accumulation increasing from valerate to acetate. It also sustains high PCO activity over 5 cycles and UV-driven photo-regeneration in clean air, with minimal activity loss due to reversible carbonaceous fouling rather than structural degradation. Combined photoelectrochemical, EPR, DRIFTS, and XPS findings further support S-scheme-like charge separation in TGBN-10, with graphite likely serving as a conductive interfacial mediator. These findings demonstrate the potential of TGBN-10 as a functional noble-metal-free photocatalyst for aldehyde VOC abatement under representative industrial/indoor-air conditions.

title: Modulating interfacial charge migration in g‑C3N4/Zn-Sr0.25H1.5Ta2O6·H2O heterostructures for accelerated drug contaminant degradation
abstract: Abstract To address the bottlenecks of low visible-light utilization, rapid carrier recombination, and insufficient active sites of pristine photocatalysts for contaminant degradation, step-scheme (S-scheme) g-C 3 N 4 /Zn-Sr 0.25 H 1.5 Ta 2 O 6 ·H 2 O photocatalysts were synthesized via a combined calcination-solvothermal method. The photocatalytic performance towards tetracycline degradation and enhancement mechanism were systematically explored by integrating multiple characterization techniques. The synthesized g-C 3 N 4 /Zn-Sr 0.25 H 1.5 Ta 2 O 6 ·H 2 O composites exhibited improved photocatalytic performance, with a maximum apparent rate constant (k) of 0.12269 min -1 , 3.69, 38.22, and 2.65 times those of Sr 0.25 H 1.5 Ta 2 O 6 ·H 2 O, g-C 3 N 4 , and binary g-C 3 N 4 /Sr 0.25 H 1.5 Ta 2 O 6 ·H 2 O, respectively. This work systematically deciphered the synergistic mechanism between Zn-doping and S-scheme heterojunction, as probed by in-situ X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) measurements that directly demonstrated the directional migration of photogenerated carriers. Zn-doping broadened the optical absorption and created more active sites for tetracycline adsorption and surface degradation reaction, while the constructed S-scheme heterostructures effectively promoted the separation and directional migration of photogenerated carriers for tetracycline degradation. This study not only provides novel theoretical insights and experimental references for the precise design and controllable synthesis of element-doped S-scheme heterojunctions but also offers a promising strategy for environmental remediation of refractory organic pollutants.

title: The role of task-specific ionic liquids in lignocellulosic biomass pretreatment and catalytic valorization
abstract: The transition to a circular bioeconomy necessitates innovative technologies capable of valorizing lignocellulosic biomass, a structurally complex and highly recalcitrant feedstock. This review critically examines the application of task-specific ionic liquids (TSILs) in the pretreatment and catalytic conversion of biomass into high-value chemicals and fuels. Through deliberate molecular design, TSILs can transform a recalcitrant waste stream into a versatile chemical resource by selectively deconstructing cellulose hydrogen-bonding networks and lignin-carbohydrate complexes. Their pivotal role is examined across three key areas: (i) Advanced fractionation, where TSILs demonstrate high technical efficiency in cellulose dissolution and lignin isolation, often at the expense of increased separation complexity. (ii) Integrated catalytic conversion, where dual solvent–catalyst systems achieve high yields of biomass-derived platform chemicals, with up to ~ 90% furfural, ~ 91% 5-HMF, and ~ 18 wt% levulinic acid, depending on TSIL class and feedstock. (iii) System sustainability, where IL-recycling efficiencies exceeding 95% over multiple cycles are attained by novel recycling protocols, including membrane-assisted and electrochemical methods, with operating costs being reduced as a result. By linking structure–function relationships to process performance, this review highlights how TSILs overcome biomass recalcitrance while also addressing the techno-economic barriers to industrial-scale implementation. Further, dedicated consideration is also given to computer-aided IL design (CAILD), double-salt task-specific ILs (DS-TSILs), and integrated molecular-process design frameworks as promising frontiers for rational TSIL engineering. We conclude that continued advances in solvent recyclability, energy efficiency, and scale-up will be decisive in translating TSIL-based biorefineries from laboratory innovation to industrial implementation in a sustainable circular economy.

title: Multifunctional transdermal nanocomposite patch based on phenolated lignin-chitosan reinforced with MgO nanoparticles for wound healing
abstract: This study reports the fabrication of chitosan-based nanocomposite films containing lignin and MgO nanoparticles for in vitro and in vivo wound-healing applications. Phenolated lignin nanoparticles (100 nm, ζ = −29 mV) enhanced antioxidant functionality, while MgO nanoparticles (192 nm, ζ = −14 mV) were incorporated as an inorganic reinforcing component. FTIR, XRD, and XPS analyses suggested changes in intermolecular interactions and local chemical environments following incorporation of lignin and MgO nanoparticles. The nanocomposites exhibited favourable physicochemical properties, including a high swelling ratio (91.6%), reduced water contact angle (41.40°), and improved tensile strength (80 MPa). They also showed strong antioxidant activity (ABTS: 325 ± 8 µg TE mL⁻¹; DPPH: 152 ± 5 µg TE mL⁻¹), high protein adsorption (2.3 g BSA g⁻¹), robust UV shielding, and > 95% inhibition of Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus. Biological evaluation demonstrated high biocompatibility (> 90% viability in HaCaT and HDF cells), low hemolysis (< 12%), and favorable blood-clotting indices (~ 40%). In vitro scratch assays showed complete wound closure within 48 h, indicating enhanced fibroblast migration. In a mouse wound model, the lead film achieved 74.1% wound closure after 15 days, compared with 63.8% for DuoDerm and 60.1% for the untreated control. Histological and immunohistochemical analyses further showed reduced residual granulation tissue, increased collagen deposition, and a nonsignificant trend toward reduced CD45-positive inflammatory-cell infiltration. The integrated formulation therefore combines structural reinforcement with antioxidant, antibacterial, cytocompatibility, and wound-repair-supporting functions in a single bio-based platform system. Overall, these findings suggest that phenolated lignin–chitosan/MgO nanocomposites are promising sustainable, multifunctional wound-dressing materials. Engineering of a multifunctional phenolated lignin-chitosan/MgO nanocomposite transdermal patch for enhanced wound healing. Phenolated kraft lignin-derived nanoparticles and MgO nanoparticles were integrated into a chitosan matrix to obtain bioactive patches with reactive oxygen species-scavenging, antibacterial, and inflammation-modulating properties, resulting in improved wound healing performance. Fakhar, A. (2026). https://BioRender.com/nvpivp4 .

title: Brittle interfacial layer suppression in Cf/C brazed joints with refractory metal via hierarchical microstructure engineering
abstract: Abstract Brazing carbon fiber reinforced carbon matrix composites (C f /C) to metals remains a core technological challenge in manufacturing high-temperature composite components for aerospace applications. Although traditional active brazing filler metals can achieve good wetting of the composites, uncontrolled interfacial reactions on the C f /C side lead to the formation of continuous brittle phases, and large residual stress undermine the reliability of the joint. In this study, a self-prepared face-centered cubic (FCC) FeCoNiAlCuTi high-entropy alloy was used as the brazing filler metal. The aim was to exploit its high mixing entropy to suppress the formation of a continuous brittle phase at the C f /C interface. Experimental results showed that the brazed seam forms a multi-layered structure, mainly composed of the C f /C side reaction zone, the Nb solid solution banded zone, and the eutectic zone. No continuous brittle layer formed at the C f /C side interface, and a gully-shaped interlocking interface was formed with the FeCoNiAl ductile phase. This strategy transfers part of the joint stress to the internal FCC phase. Finite element simulations indicated that the peak Mises stress was reduced from 371 MPa to 274 MPa. Under the optimal brazing parameters of 1340 ℃ for 20 min, the shear strength of the joint reaches 40.7 MPa. Briefly stated, this study alleviated the initiation and growth of brittle reactive layers at the interface of C f /C composites, providing important support for the development of high-performance bonding processes for C f /C composites and facilitating their practical application in high-temperature aerospace components.

title: Polymeric micelles as drug delivery nanosystems: Moving towards improved stability
abstract: Polymeric micelles (PMs) have been identified as promising systems for nanodrug delivery due to their high solubilizing power, small size, long shelf life, good biocompatibility and high drug loading capacity. Despite their promising properties, PMs’ clinical translation remains hindered by two main challenges, instability under physiological conditions and regulatory requirements. Upon intravenous administration, PMs encounter a dynamic biological environment characterized by significant dilution, abrupt changes in pH, enzyme and ionic strength, contact with various macromolecules (proteins, lipids), and shear forces that affect their surface properties. These changes can disrupt the balance of the PM system, compromising the integrity of the micelles. Several attempts have been made to avoid these changes, including cross-linking approaches, stimuli-responsive PMs and polymer-drug conjugates. This review provides an insight into the most promising techniques to improve micelle stability and drug retention, enhancing the therapeutic efficacy of drugs and paving the way for PMs’ clinical translation.

title: Dual-anchored interfacial and sheet-sphere hybrid network engineering for thermally conductive, mechanically robust EVA/BN photovoltaic encapsulants
abstract: Abstract Encapsulation films combining high thermal conductivity, stable electrical insulation, and excellent mechanical properties are urgently needed for photovoltaic modules. However, achieving all these properties simultaneously in conventional ethylene–vinyl acetate copolymer (EVA) encapsulants remains a significant challenge. Herein, a synergistic three-tier strategy integrating EVA matrix crosslinking, a sheet-sphere hybrid filler network, and dual-anchored interfacial engineering is proposed to resolve this conflict. Specifically, 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane (KH550) is grafted onto both the EVA matrix and the boron nitride (BN) filler surfaces via radical coupling and hydroxylation, respectively, establishing a dual-anchored interface of covalent bonds and hydrogen bonds. Combined with a sheet-sphere hybrid BN architecture (f-BN) constructed from hexagonal boron nitride microplatelets and spherical boron nitride microspheres, and a crosslinked EVA matrix (cEVA), this design enables the as-prepared cEVA/f-BN composite encapsulation film to achieve a high through-plane thermal conductivity‌ of 2.96 W·m⁻ 1 ·K⁻ 1 , representing a 1245% enhancement compared to the pure EVA film. Remarkably, the composite maintains a tensile strength of 8.99 MPa, an elongation of 89.75% at a filler loading of 110 phr, and a volume resistivity exceeding 10 14 Ω·cm. The composite film also exhibits high solar reflectance (91.09%) and infrared emissivity (96.17%), which in synergy with its enhanced thermal conductivity, reduce the photovoltaic module temperature by 5.34 ℃.This study not only demonstrates a good combination of thermal and mechanical properties in EVA encapsulants but also provides a broadly applicable interfacial design reference for the development of polymer composite materials that require both heat dissipation, mechanical strength, and electrical insulation.

title: 2D˗on˗2D vertically–horizontally oriented SnS2˗Ti3C2Tx MXene heterostructures with sulfur vacancies for high-energy asymmetric supercapacitors
abstract: Rationally designed heterostructures hold significant promise for next-generation energy storage devices because their synergistically integrated features generally outperform those of pristine materials. However, achieving rational heterostructure design with precise structural control remains a major challenge that limits the electrochemical potential. In this study, well-defined vertically aligned two-dimensional (2D) SnS 2 nanosheets were anchored onto horizontally oriented 2D Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene microflakes to form a 2D-on-2D heterostructure. The inherently low electrical conductivity of SnS 2 was effectively addressed through sulfur vacancy (S v ) engineering, resulting in highly energetic vertical–horizontal 2D˗on˗2D S v –SnS 2 –Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene heterostructures. Density functional theory calculations confirmed the enhanced electronic conductivity and strong Na + adsorption, which facilitated rapid ion transport and superior electrochemical performance. These synergistic effects optimized the S v –SnS 2 –Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene heterostructure, exhibiting high specific capacitance (706 F g -1 at 2 A g -1 ) and excellent cycling stability. The assembled asymmetric supercapacitor, employing S v –SnS 2 –Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene as the cathode and Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene as the anode, delivered an exceptional energy density of 58.33 Wh kg -1 at a power density of 800 W Kg -1 , while retaining ~96% of its capacitance after 10,000 cycles. This study presents a scalable strategy for constructing defect-engineered 2D˗on˗2D heterostructures, thereby advancing the development of next-generation high-performance energy storage devices. This study highlights well-defined, vertically aligned two-dimensional (2D) SnS 2 nanosheets anchored on horizontally oriented 2D Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene microflakes to form a robust 2D-on-2D heterostructure. Sulfur vacancy (S v ) engineering significantly enhances the SnS 2 electrical conductivity, enabling highly energetic 2D-on-2D S v –SnS 2 –Ti 3 C 2 T x MXene heterostructures with high electrochemical energy storage performance

title: 2D Ti3C2Tx-MXene-patterned electrode enables highly sensitive humidity sensing
abstract: Flexible, metal-free humidity sensors with high sensitivity, linear impedance response, and fast response/recovery times are vital for next-generation wearable electronics and environmental monitoring, whereas poor linearity limits the rapid and precise detection of humidity. Here, we report a metal-free humidity sensor that integrates lithographically patterned two-dimensional (2D) Ti 3 C 2 T x -MXene nanosheets (2DMS) interdigital electrodes (IDEs) with an engineered ultrathin network of 2D anatase TiO 2 nanosheets (2DTS) as the active humidity-responsive layer on a cyclic olefin copolymer (COC) substrate. The solution-processed 2DMS IDEs provide high electrical conductivity, mechanical robustness, and scalable patterning, while the 2DTS film forms a continuous, hydroxyl-rich, chemically robust surface network for reversible water adsorption and rapid proton-mediated transport. The resulting 2DMS@2DTS sensor exhibits highly linear and reversible impedance and capacitance modulation across a broad humidity range (6–86% RH), with low hysteresis, minimal change over 24 h, and a sensitivity of 4.41 × 10 5 Ω/%RH at 1 kHz. COMSOL-assisted finite element method (FEM) simulations reveal humidity-induced dielectric redistribution in the IDE’s electric field, while density functional theory (DFT) calculations demonstrate a reduced activation energy for proton (H⁺) migration under humid conditions. These theoretical insights are in excellent agreement with the experimentally observed fast, repeatable response and recovery characteristics, thereby providing a mechanistic understanding of the device’s high-performance humidity-sensing behavior. Owing to its all-2D-materials architecture and flexible COC substrate, the sensor enables practical applications, including real-time physiological monitoring. This work introduces a smart strategy that couples patterned 2DMS electrodes with engineered 2DTS to achieve scalable, metal-free, and flexible humidity sensors, providing a promising platform for wearable and intelligent sensing systems.

title: Morphology-engineered ZIF-8-derived porous carbon for high-performance solar thermochemical energy storage
abstract: Porous carbon derived from metal-organic frameworks holds immense potential for solar thermochemical energy storage (STES) owing to its high surface area and tunable pore structure. Nevertheless, the lack of elucidation regarding the mechanism by which nano-carrier morphology regulates the STES performance of hydrated salt composites contradicts its versatile applications. Herein, a morphological engineering strategy was employed to synthesize zeolite imidazolate framework (ZIF-8)-derived porous carbon with five different morphologies (rhombic dodecahedron, cube, plate, interpenetrating 36-faced twin, and rod) as adsorption carriers. Furthermore, a systematic investigation was conducted into the structure-property relationship among the carrier morphology, pore structure, and STES performance. Thanks to the loose packing and anti-agglomeration achieved through its locally concave geometric features and hierarchical microporous/mesoporous structure of ITZAC2, the LM2/ITZAC2-60 composite exhibits high moisture absorption capacity, storage density (1407.5 kJ·kg − 1 ), and good operational reliability (95.2% capacity retention after 20-cycle testing), while also demonstrating favorable solar-to-thermal conversion characteristics and heat transfer capability. This work not only reveals the critical mechanisms governing the role of carrier morphology in STES performance, offering a novel strategy for morphological engineering in the rational design of high-performance heat storage materials, but also provides a future-oriented proposition for the implementation of STES materials in buildings.

title: Suppressing ionic percolation in ultralow-loss SiO₂/glass composite low-temperature co-fired ceramics through quartz/cristobalite phase engineering for mmwave radio frequency filter applications
abstract: Low-temperature co-fired ceramics (LTCCs) are widely utilized in millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication modules, owing to their excellent dielectric properties and process compatibility. With the rapid advancement of mmWave communication, low-loss LTCCs have become increasingly important for minimizing insertion loss and signal attenuation in mmWave frequency range. Among the various candidates in LTCC compositions, SiO₂-based glass/ceramic filler composites have attracted considerable attention, owing to their low dielectric constant and glass-assisted densification behavior under low-temperature sintering process. However, despite the strong influence of glass-phase transformations on dielectric loss characteristics, systematic studies on the underlying mechanisms remain limited. Herein, we systematically investigate phase engineering in SiO₂-based glass/ceramic filler composites to achieve ultralow dielectric loss while maintaining comparable sintered density, thereby clarifying the effects of glass-phase transitions on dielectric-loss behavior. With increasing sintering temperature, the crystalline phases evolved from quartz to mixed quartz–cristobalite and finally to cristobalite structures. In particular, the quartz–cristobalite mixed-phase sample sintered at 900 °C exhibited superior dielectric properties and the most stable dielectric-loss characteristics, showing a dielectric constant of 4.5, an ultralow dielectric loss of 0.0006, and a high Q × f value of 20,400 GHz, outperforming previously reported glass-based LTCC materials. These enhanced dielectric properties were attributed to suppression of ionic percolation during the crystallization of mixed phases consisting of quartz and cristobalite structures. Finally, a multilayer-integrated mmWave (~ 28 GHz) RF filter chip was successfully fabricated using the developed LTCC material. The fabricated device exhibited stable band-pass filtering characteristics near 28 GHz, achieving a low insertion loss of 0.9 dB and an exceptional figure of merit (FoM) of 325.7, outperforming previously reported LTCC-based RF filter materials. These findings provide an insight into the design of low-permittivity LTCC systems through glass phase-engineered dielectric control.

title: Bioinspired microactuators fabricated via one-step meniscus-guided 3D nanoprinting
abstract: Abstract We introduce a bioinspired microactuator fabricated via a one-step meniscus-guided 3D nanoprinting technique. This technique directly produces a freestanding three-dimensional composite architecture by integrating a rigid nanoparticle framework with a hygroscopic polymer matrix in a single, assembly-free process. Inspired by the functional integration of rigid and compliant components in insect exoskeletal joint, our design synergistically combines load-bearing strength and humidity-driven swelling in a single microscale pillar. Comprehensive experiments, including comparative control structures and microscopic analysis, elucidated the actuation mechanism: the nanoparticle scaffold provides mechanical support while the polymeric phase provides volumetric expansion, yielding large reversible elongation under humidity with preserved structural integrity. The resulting AuNP–PVP microactuator shows humidity-responsive actuation at the microscale, with representative demonstrations of repeated humidity cycling and load lifting up to approximately 800 times its estimated own weight under the tested conditions. Variant geometries such as hinged pillars demonstrate how axial swelling can be converted into bending motion, and an optical configuration shows how actuation can modulate reflected light signals. This nanoprinting approach provides a simple strategy for constructing bioinspired soft microactuators with humidity-responsive deformation and potential applicability in microscale sensing, optical modulation, and adaptive microdevices.

title: Valorization of elemental sulfur via catalyst-free polymerization into dynamic poly(glycerol-sulfur) nano-networks for antibacterial and antiviral applications
abstract: Abstract The growing threat of antimicrobial resistance and viral infections has intensified the demand for adaptive biomaterials that combine intrinsic bioactivity with controlled therapeutic delivery. In parallel, the development of sustainable polymeric materials from abundant and underutilized feedstocks has become an increasingly important objective. Elemental sulfur, an industrial byproduct produced on a megaton scale, represents a highly attractive yet largely untapped building block for functional polymer synthesis. Herein, we report a one-pot, catalyst- and solvent-free copolymerization of glycidol with elemental sulfur to generate poly(glycerol-sulfur) (hPG-Sn), comprising polyglycerol and polysulfide segments. This approach provides a modular route to sulfur-containing polymers while valorizing elemental sulfur as a sustainable feedstock. The resulting polymers spontaneously form nanoscale networks (200–500 nm) in aqueous media. Importantly, the dynamic S–S bonds within the polysulfide segments impart a stimuli-responsive architecture that enables reversible opening and closing of the network pores, thereby facilitating drug loading and subsequent encapsulation and release. Tetracycline-loaded hPG-Sn networks exhibited a ten-fold enhancement in antibacterial efficacy compared with the free drug, while maintaining low cytotoxicity toward human cells. The chemical modularity of the polysulfide domains further enables facile post-functionalization through thiol-disulfide exchange. Functionalization with 11-mercaptoundecanesulfonate (MUS) generated negatively charged nanoparticles (~ 550 nm, ζ = −30 mV) that exhibited pronounced antiviral activity against herpes simplex virus (HSV), including both inhibitory and virucidal effects. Thus, hPG-Sn combines sustainable sulfur utilization, dynamic and reversible pore modulation, efficient therapeutic cargo loading, and facile surface functionalization within a single polymer platform. These features highlight its potential as an adaptable nanomaterial for controlled antimicrobial and antiviral delivery.

title: A comprehensive review of advanced manufacturing techniques, ai-enabled design, and mechanical characterization of nature-inspired helicoidal hybrid composites for impact-resistant applications
abstract: Abstract Helicoidal structures mimic nature and are evident in plant cell walls, lamellar bone, and the shell structures of mantis shrimp and beetles. These nature-inspired helicoidal composites are widely used in impact-resistant applications. Traditional hand-layup methods for producing layered helicoidal composites can introduce defects such as gaps, overlaps, and wrinkles, which can be mitigated using Automated Fiber Placement (AFP). Optimizing AFP process parameters, including pressure, temperature, and layup speed, is crucial. While experimental optimization is costly and time-consuming, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based design offers a more efficient alternative. This narrative review explores the inspiration behind helicoidal structures and their application fields. It also covers advanced manufacturing of hybrid long-fiber layered composites using AFP + autoclave/hot press, ceramic filler-based nanocomposites using direct ink writing (DIW), and multi-walled carbon nanotube (MWCNT)-based nanocomposites using digital micromirror device (DMD). Furthermore, it discusses the roles of machine learning and deep learning, coupled with finite element modeling, in minimizing process-induced defects. Compared with conventional AFP inspection techniques such as laser profilometry and thermography, a defect-detection algorithm based on PointNet + + , a convolutional neural network (CNN), can be tailored for 3D point cloud segmentation, offering a cost-effective, user-friendly alternative. Next, the mechanical and microstructural properties of helicoidal composites, compared with those of traditional laminates, are discussed to evalaute impact performance. Helicoidal composites with low inter-ply angles up to 20° consistently outperform conventional lay-ups under quasi-static and impact loading, due to a crack-twisting mechanism and superior out-of-plane properties. Incorporating nylon 6 powder microparticles into carbon/epoxy and glass/epoxy helicoidal composites subjected to impact loading significantly improves their toughness through self-healing, compared with virgin helicoidal composites. Carbon/epoxy helicoidal composites with low inter-ply angles of up to 9° are prone to extensive matrix cracking and minor fiber damage, while self-healing in carbon/epoxy composites also helps minimize matrix cracking but does not reduce fiber damage. In contrast, self-healing significantly decreases overall damage in glass/epoxy composites. Self-healing is more effective at eliminating damage in glass/epoxy than in carbon/epoxy, primarily because the former exhibits higher ductility (% elongation) than the latter.

title: Cold sintering process induces dielectric resonance in Mo-MXene/ReFeOx (Re = Ce, Er, Gd) sintered body for EMW absorption
abstract: Dielectric resonance arises from the collective oscillation of local electrons between adjacent, non-contacting particles under an external alternating electric field. Adjusting the spacing between particles to induce a dielectric response is crucial for electromagnetic wave (EMW) absorption capability. This work introduces an innovative cold press sintering (CSP) technique conducive to generating dielectric resonance; this method effectively anchors rare-earth (RE) magnetic nanoparticles onto a two-dimensional (2D) Mo-MXene conductive substrate while allowing for the controllable adjustment of the spacing between nanoparticles. Furthermore, compared to high-temperature sintering, low-temperature CSP mitigates the oxidation of Mo-MXene nanosheets, preserves their high electrical conductivity, and facilitates electron supply to the loaded magnetic nanoparticles. Experimental results and theoretical simulations demonstrate that Mo-MXene/ReFeO x (Re = Ce, Er, Gd) exhibits distinct dielectric resonance characteristics, thereby enabling the modulation of dielectric resonance-type loss in RE magnetic materials. Additionally, Mo-MXene/ReFeO x maintains excellent magnetic stability across various temperatures.
