This technique demonstrates versatility, as dielectric resonance phenomena, and the resulting superior EMW absorption performance, are observed in Mo-MXene/CeFeO x , Mo-MXene/ErFeO x , and Mo-MXene/GdFeO x sintered bodies, with reflection loss ( R L ) values of -49.69 dB, -33.18 dB, and − 40.13 dB, respectively. Radar cross-section (RCS) simulations indicate that Mo-MXene/ReFeO x sintered bodies inherit practical potential for radar stealth applications. In summary, this work breaks through the traditional paradigm of relaxation loss modulation and offers a novel perspective for the design of dielectric resonance-type EMW absorption materials.

title: Fabrication of large-sized robust carbon aerogel composites via pre-shrinkage-induced interfacial engineering
abstract: Abstract We report a strategy for synthesizing crack-free carbon aerogel (CA) composites by rationally matching the carbonization shrinkage of viscose fiber felts (VFs) with that of a phenolic resin (PR) aerogel matrix. The VFs were pretreated at elevated temperatures to induce controlled pre-shrinkage, followed by an in situ sol-gel transition and ambient-pressure drying of the PR precursor to produce large monolithic organic aerogels. By selecting a pretreatment temperature of 265 °C, the fibers and the matrix showed nearly identical subsequent carbonization shrinkages (26.2% versus 25.0%). This matched shrinkage drastically reduced residual stress, yielding a defect content of only 2% and a continuous, gradient interface without cracks or voids. The optimal composite achieved specific compressive and flexural strengths of 106.9 and 29.1 MPa·g − 1 ·cm 3 , respectively, along with a fracture toughness of 0.54 MPa·m 1/2 , significantly outperforming composites with mismatched shrinkages. Compared with conventional non-pre-shrunk counterparts, this design achieves a 91% reduction in residual stress and a 94% decrease in structural defects, resulting in 3.0-fold and 2.5-fold improvements in specific compressive and flexural strengths, respectively, as well as a 2.3-fold increase in fracture toughness. The design principle was further exploited to tune the matrix microstructure and density, and the material retained its structural integrity and superior high-temperature mechanical properties even at 1800 °C. This work demonstrates that controlling the shrinkage compatibility between reinforcement and matrix provides a versatile route to high-performance, large-sized CA composites for demanding structural and thermal applications.

title: Glycine-based piezoelectric nanogenerators for mechanodynamic tissue regeneration
abstract: The rapid growth of wearable and implantable electronics has led to a search for power systems that are safe for the body and can disappear when no longer needed. Glycine-based piezoelectric nanogenerators (PENGs) have become a leading option in this area because they naturally generate electricity from movement, have a simple structure, and are fully biodegradable. This review provides a detailed look at glycine PENGs, moving from basic crystal science to their use in tissue engineering. We first look at how glycine turns mechanical energy into electricity, focusing on its different crystal forms and how they are built into structures such as tiny tubes, reinforced materials, and fibrous materials. A major part of this discussion is how these devices can both sense body movement and actively help tissues heal. Beyond just collecting energy, we explain how glycine itself helps the body, such as by controlling immune responses and protecting cells. We also study how the mechanodynamic processes of these devices, specifically how their physical motion and resulting electricity guide cell growth and regulate mechanotransduction signaling. Finally, we show examples of how this technology helps regenerate nerves, muscles, skin, and bone, while discussing the practical steps needed to ensure their biocompatibility in the body. This review positions glycine PENGs as one of the key technologies for future self-powered medical devices for tissue healing and regenerative purposes.

title: Structure and performance study of iPP microporous membrane derived from β-transcrystalline precursor for lithium-ion battery separators
abstract: A β-transcrystalline (β-TC) polypropylene microporous membrane fabricated by synchronous biaxial stretching of a precursor film with continuous and ordered β-transcrystallinity was evaluated as a lithium-ion battery separator, with a conventional β-spherocrystalline (β-SC) membrane as the comparative sample. The β-TC separator exhibited greater elongation at break than its counterpart and favorable elastic recovery under compressive stress, and its maximum puncture force was approximately twice that of its counterpart. It also maintained structural integrity and microporosity to higher temperatures, with a considerably lower degree of thermal shrinkage. EIS measurements revealed that the β-TC separator possessed higher ionic conductivity and lower bulk resistance than its counterpart. In LiFePO₄/Li half-cells, the β-TC separator delivered superior rate capability, with the capacity gap widening at elevated C-rates, and its capacity retention over 200 cycles was 78.6%, compared with 54.0% for the β-SC separator. These performance advantages are attributed to the uniformly fine fibrillar network and narrow pore size distribution of the β-TC membrane, which provide more efficient ion transport pathways and consequently enable superior rate capability and cycling stability in the cells.

title: Deep eutectic solvent-mediated multiscale silk fibroin hybrid eutectogels with broadly tunable mechanics for flexible electronics and energy harvesting
abstract: Abstract Developing sustainable hybrid gels with simultaneous tunability and extensibility remains challenging due to the lack of hierarchical network design and synergistic interfacial interactions. Here, we introduce a deep eutectic solvent (DES)-mediated multiscale regulation (DMR) strategy to construct hierarchical networks with synergistic interaction for achieving broadly tunable mechanical properties in biomass-derived hybrid eutectogels. Using Bombyx mori silk fibroin (SF) as a model, DES hierarchically deconstructs macroscopic SF across micro-, nano-, and molecular scales. These multiscale structural units serve as hierarchical reinforcements within the polymer matrix, forming a synergistic hybrid network stabilized by multiple hydrogen bonds and electrostatic interactions. Consequently, the resulting multiscale hybrid eutectogels exhibit broadly tunable mechanical properties, with tensile strength spanning nearly two orders of magnitude (0.02–1.6 MPa) and modulus nearly three orders of magnitude (0.008–3.5 MPa), alongside excellent ionic conductivity and multifunctionality. Molecular dynamics simulations and spectroscopic analyses provide evidence supporting the proposed multiscale interfacial interaction mechanisms. Furthermore, we demonstrate proof-of-concept applications of these hybrid materials in advanced soft electronics, including an ultra-conformable wearable sensor for physiological monitoring and a load-bearing triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) for self-powered systems. This multiscale composite design strategy offers a promising approach toward developing versatile biomass-based hybrid materials, with potential utility in flexible electronics and energy-harvesting devices.

title: Gecko-inspired tunable hierarchical interface for CF/PEEK-titanium hybrid laminates: synergistic enhancement via laser-induced micro-texturing and in-situ grown TiO2 nanotube arrays
abstract: A hierarchical micro-nano structure inspired by geckos was constructed on the titanium surface via laser-induced micro-texturing and in-situ growth of TiO2 nanotube arrays (TNTs). An effective strategy was proposed to enhance the interfacial bonding performance of carbon fiber reinforced polyetheretherketone-titanium (CF/PEEK-titanium) hybrid laminates. The influence of microgroove depth and spacing on the interfacial performance was studied, and highly ordered TNTs were fabricated using a two-step anodic oxidation process. The surface morphology, physical and chemical properties, surface wettability and interlayer bonding performance of the treated titanium plate were investigated. The results showed that highly uniform and ordered TNTs successfully formed in the microgrooves and on the surface. Within the investigated parameter range, the optimal performance is achieved at a groove depth of 15 μm and a groove spacing of 1.0 mm. Under this condition, the water contact angle decreased to 14.59°, the surface free energy reached 83.25 mJ/m2, and the apparent interlaminar shear strength (ILSS) attains 88.39 MPa, corresponding to a 201.98% increase relative to the untreated laminate. The fracture surface observation revealed PEEK retention within the laser-induced micro-texturing and provided morphological evidence suggesting possible PEEK penetration into the TNT nanopores, forming a multiscale mechanical interlocking effect, which transformed the dominant failure mode from interfacial delamination to cohesive and mixed failure modes. The synergistic effects of microscale interlocking, nanoscale anchoring, improved wettability and increased effective bonding area collectively contributed to the significant enhancement in interfacial strength. This study provides an integrated and controllable micro-nano interface engineering approach for manufacturing CF/PEEK-titanium hybrid laminates with excellent interlaminar behavior. A gecko-inspired hierarchical interface was constructed on titanium sheets. Laser-texturing and TiO2 nanotube arrays enable multiscale anchoring. The hierarchical interface improved ILSS by 201.98%, from 29.27 MPa to 88.39 MPa. Multiscale interlocking transformed failure from debonding to mixed failure.

title: Interfacial stabilization of Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene via lysozyme amyloid coating for durable flexible strain sensing
abstract: Two-dimensional Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene holds great promise for flexible conductive hydrogel sensing owing to its exceptional electrical conductivity and solution processability; however, its rapid oxidative degradation in aqueous environments severely limits long-term service stability. Herein, we propose an interfacial stabilization strategy: by exploiting tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP)-induced phase transition of lysozyme, a dense protein amyloid-like aggregate (PTL) protective coating is assembled in situ on Ti₃C₂Tₓ nanosheet surfaces, yielding PTL@Ti₃C₂Tₓ with excellent chemical stability and a high hydrogel conductivity of 94.5 mS cm⁻¹. Density functional theory calculations reveal that lysozyme residues bind spontaneously to Ti₃C₂Tₓ terminations through hydrogen bonding and electrostatic interactions, providing a molecular basis for the conformal coating, whose antioxidant protection was further verified by spectroscopic, elemental, and electrical analyses. A PVA/cellulose nanofiber composite hydrogel sensor (PCPT) constructed with PTL@Ti₃C₂Tₓ exhibited a fracture strain of 584%, tensile strength of 1.60 MPa, toughness of 5.25 MJ m⁻³, and a gauge factor of 4.27. More importantly, PCPT maintained stable sensing functionality after 90 days of storage, surpassing the unmodified counterpart. This work offers a green and effective strategy for enhancing the long-term stability of Ti₃C₂Tₓ in flexible electronics and wearable sensing.

title: Bio-inspired eutectic gel with muscle-fascia-like recovery for high-performance wearable strain sensor
abstract: Eutectic gels are attractive for wearable strain sensors because of their ionic conductivity and environmental stability, but their low strength and incomplete recovery under repeated loading limit long-term use. Inspired by the sandwich structure of skeletal muscle and fascia, we report a composite (NF-Gel) in which an electrospun thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) nanofiber (NF) membrane is embedded between layers of a ZnCl 2 -ethylene glycol/poly(acrylic acid) eutectic gel. The non-polymerizable DES remains a continuous ion-conducting phase after curing, giving a conductivity of 11.01 mS cm − 1 . Rapid precursor infiltration into membrane and fiber swelling create an interpenetrated fiber-gel interface. A 109 μm NF membrane, occupying about 5% of the sensor thickness, raises the tensile strength 11-fold to 1.05 MPa and the toughness 9-fold to 7.17 MJ m −3 while preserving an elongation of 1200%. After an initial Mullins-type softening, the composite reached a stable cyclic response of over 3000 sensing cycles. The sensor operates over a range of 0-1200% strain with gauge factors of 2.16, 3.846 and 1.65 in three linear regions and response and recovery times of 0.156 and 0.231 s, and detects facial expressions, joint motion and speech with signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) of 32.8–45.3 dB. NF-Gel also adheres to diverse substrates (461–849 kPa), maintains over 95% keratinocyte viability, inhibits Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus , and shows flame resistance. A temperature coefficient of resistance of -0.46% / o C enables fire warning and fever monitoring, and the strain-temperature cross-sensitivity is quantified.

title: CO2 mineralization-integrated 3D printed concrete: Review and challenges
abstract: 3D printed concrete (3DPC) faces a substantial carbon emission challenge due to its high binder content. CO 2 mineralization provides a promising route for simultaneous carbon sequestration and performance enhancement. This paper reviews CO 2 mineralization-integrated 3DPC technology, with emphasis on recent progress, key mechanisms, and remaining challenges. The review establishes a material–process–performance–sustainability framework to examine mineralization mechanisms across different material systems, including cement-based systems, supplementary and novel cementitious materials, and aggregates as mineralization carriers. It also compares the major integration pathways, including plastic-state mineralization, hardening-stage CO 2 curing, and material precarbonation. Plastic-state mineralization is effective for rheological regulation and buildability enhancement, but its carbon uptake is generally limited by short reaction time and gas utilization efficiency. Hardening-stage CO 2 curing can achieve higher carbon uptake and stronger microstructural densification, yet it is constrained by diffusion depth, moisture gradients, and scale-up difficulty. Available evidence indicates that CO 2 mineralization can improve printability, mechanical strength, and interlayer bonding through accelerated hydration, carbonate precipitation, and pore refinement. However, non-uniform reactions, increased anisotropy, durability uncertainty, and additional energy or cost demands remain major barriers. This review highlights that the future development of CO 2 mineralization-integrated 3DPC should move from isolated performance optimization toward coordinated control of material reactivity, CO 2 transport, printing process, long-term durability, and net life-cycle benefit.

title: Comparative surface engineering of nickel-loaded calcium-aluminum layered double oxide for enhanced methanation: citric acid treatment versus Fe doping
abstract: The Sabatier reaction, leading to the catalytic hydrogenation of carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) to methane (CH 4 ), offers a practical route to synthetic natural gas compatible with existing infrastructure. Yet, widespread adoption requires low-cost catalysts that combine favorable kinetics, high CH 4 selectivity, and productivity under demanding throughput. Herein, a non-precious nickel (Ni)/calcium-aluminum (CaAl)-layered double oxide (LDO) platform (NCL) is investigated using two deliberately separated modification routes: organic acid treatment and metal doping. Citric acid treatment (C-NCL) increases Ni dispersion and modifies the Ni-support interfacial environment, whereas iron (Fe) doping predominantly alters reducibility, defect-related properties, and surface basic site distribution. C-NCL achieves 66.6% CO 2 conversion with 96.5% CH 4 selectivity at 400 °C. At 350 °C, C-NCL reaches 44.9% CO₂ conversion, lower than several reference catalysts; its high-WHSV productivity is attributed to the test conditions rather than intrinsic catalytic superiority. These results clarify how citric acid treatment and Fe doping independently tune the Ni–support interface. Differential measurements at 5 mg catalyst loading yield apparent activation energies (E a, app ) of 94.6, 53.6, and 72.6 kJ mol − 1 for NCL, C-NCL, and Fe-NCL, respectively, showing that both routes lower the apparent kinetic barrier relative to NCL, with the largest decrease for C-NCL. In-situ diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy reveals carbonate- and formate (HCOO − )-related surface species together with CH 4 formation, consistent with HCOO − involvement but not establishing its kinetic dominance; a carbon monoxide (CO)-mediated contribution cannot be excluded. This study provides a strategy-resolved comparison of two independent modification routes on a fixed Ni/CaAl-LDO platform for enhanced catalytic activity and selectivity.

title: NiCo alloys anchored on N-doped carbon nanotubes as efficient bifunctional electrocatalysts for overall water splitting
abstract: Abstract Developing the highly active, earth-abundant and stable bifunctional electrocatalysts for both oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) are crucial to overall water splitting. In this study, the microflower-like NiCo-based layered double hydroxide (NiCo-LDH) was synthesized via a hydrothermal method and subsequently converted into NiCo alloy nanoparticles anchored on nitrogen-doped carbon nanotubes (NiCo@NCNTs) through the calcination treatment. By precisely controlling the Co doping amount, a series of NiCo@NCNTs samples with tunable Ni/Co molar ratios were synthesized. Electrochemical characterizations reveal that the optimal NiCo@NCNT catalyst exhibits an exceptionally bifunctional catalytic activity, achieving low overpotentials of 295 mV (OER) and 255 mV (HER) at a current density of 10 mA cm − 2 , with the corresponding Tafel slopes of 78 mV dec − 1 and 116 mV dec − 1 , respectively. When integrated into water electrolyzer, the NiCo@NCNT-based system requires a cell voltage of 1.70 V to drive the current density of 10 mA cm − 2 , with a stable operation for over 18 hours. The remarkable catalytic performance can be primarily attributed to the incorporation of NCNTs, which not only effectively improve the dispersion of NiCo active sites but also accelerate the charge transfer.

title: Carbondot-containing sustainable polymer composites: a review of systems from processing to applications
abstract: Abstract This article reviews recent progress and existing knowledge gaps in carbon dot (CD)-containing polymer composites, emphasizing the significance of CD surface functionality and its interactions with polymer groups for developing sustainable composites with enhanced performance. It provides a comprehensive overview of the fundamental science of CDs, their synthesis techniques, and their role in sustainability. The review discusses key aspects of processing, characterization, properties, and applications of these composites, guiding future advancements in sustainable polymeric materials. It also highlights the importance of CD dispersion, interfacial bonding with polymer matrices, and the effects of crosslinking on property improvements across fields such as packaging, coatings, environmental remediation, electronics, and biomedicine. The paper notes the limited commercialization of CDs and their composites, pointing out the challenge of developing scalable, cost-effective, solvent-free production methods. It advocates for integrating synthesis science with process engineering, life-cycle assessment, techno-economic analysis, and application validation. This research proposes that future research should focus on establishing reproducible relationships between synthesis, structure, properties, and processing that can be translated into environmentally sustainable manufacturing processes. Overall, this article offers new perspectives on designing CD-based sustainable polymer composites for a broad range of applications.

title: Pore-preserving BN-coated rGO composites for heat spreading and EMI shielding
abstract: The increasing use of flexible and wearable electronics requires thermal management materials that can spread localized heat while maintaining mechanical stability and electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding performance. In this study, a flexible multifunctional heat spreader was fabricated using a reduced graphene oxide aerogel-based composite structure. First, a reduced graphene oxide aerogel was used as a continuous conductive framework for EMI shielding. To stabilize this fragile framework and improve heat transport, a thermoplastic polyurethane/boron nitride coating layer was formed on the aerogel surface without fully blocking the internal pores. The open pores of the coated framework were then filled with a hybrid filler composed of polydopamine-treated boron nitride and reduced graphene oxide aerogel flakes. In this hybrid filler, r educed graphene oxide aerogel flakes provided additional electrically conductive networks for EMI shielding, while polydopamine-treated boron nitride supplied thermally conductive filler components for heat spreading. The polydopamine layer improved the contact between boron nitride and reduced graphene oxide-based components, supporting the formation of a connected filler network. After hot pressing, the optimized composite exhibited an in-plane thermal conductivity of 7.35 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ and a through-plane thermal conductivity of 1.28 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹. It also achieved an EMI shielding effectiveness of 41.2 dB in the X-band range, along with a tensile strength of 17.5 MPa. These results show that the combined aerogel framework, coating layer, and pore-filling hybrid filler structure is effective for flexible heat spreaders requiring heat dissipation, EMI shielding, and mechanical stability.

title: In-situ engineering of a defect-rich TiO₂ interphase coupled with sulfur vacancies in WS2/TiO2@C heterostructures for enhanced Li⁺ storage in 3D-printed anodes
abstract: Tungsten disulfide (WS₂) is a promising anode material for lithium-ion batteries due to its high theoretical capacity, however, its practical application is limited by poor intrinsic conductivity and severe volume variation during cycling. Herein, we develop a 3D printable WS₂/TiO 2 @C anode (3DP-WTCN) via sulfur vacancy activation and in-situ interphase engineering. In this system, sulfur vacancy enriched WS₂ provides abundant Li⁺ adsorption sites and accelerates reaction kinetics. Meanwhile, Ti 3 C 2 T x undergoes partial transformation to form a defect-rich TiO 2 interphase, accompanied by Ti–S-related interfacial interactions, which promote interfacial coupling between WS₂ and the Ti-containing phase. This interphase regulated heterostructure promotes efficient electron transport and facilitates rapid Li⁺ diffusion while mitigating structural degradation. Importantly, the interphase regulated system is integrated with 3D-printed electrode architecture, enabling interconnected conductive pathways, shortened ion diffusion distances, and high mass loading capability. As a result, the 3DP-WTCN anode exhibits 200–500% improvement in areal capacity as compared to WTCN, WS₂ and Ti₃C₂Tₓ anode. The WTCN anode delivers a reversible capacity of 697.1 mAh g⁻¹ at 0.2 A g⁻¹ with 80.2% capacity, corresponding to improvements of ~ 248% over pristine WS₂ and ~ 365% over Ti₃C₂Tₓ MXene, while the 3DP-WTCN anode further exhibits an additional average ~ 50% increase in specific capacity compared to the WTCN anode.

title: Emerging MOF/COF-based platforms for sample preparation and detection of bisphenols in food
abstract: Bisphenols (BPs) are widely used industrial chemicals commonly detected in food matrices due to their migration from packaging materials. As endocrine-disrupting compounds, BPs can pose potential risks to human health even at trace levels, making their reliable determination in food critical. However, the effective enrichment and detection of BPs remain challenging due to their low concentrations and complex sample matrices. In recent years, metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) and covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as promising materials for sample pretreatment, sensor detection, and mass spectrometry analysis (e.g., MALDI) due to their large specific surface area, tunable pore structure, and abundant functional groups. These materials provide strong host–guest interactions and efficient mass transfer, thereby improving extraction, enrichment, and matrix cleanup of bisphenols in sample pretreatment techniques. They have also been widely applied in detection techniques, including chromatography, sensing, mass spectrometry, and other analytical methods. This review summarizes the preparation strategies, structural characteristics, and applications of MOF- and COF-based materials in different pretreatment techniques, such as solid-phase extraction, dispersive solid-phase extraction, magnetic micro-dispersive solid-phase extraction, and microextraction methods, as well as their roles in sensing and mass spectrometry. Additionally, the current challenges and future perspectives of MOF/COF-based materials in food safety monitoring are discussed, offering insights into the development of more efficient analytical materials. Magnetic MOFs enable fast m-µ-dSPE of bisphenols from food matrices. Amino-MOFs improve dSPE enrichment of bisphenols in complex foods. Imine COFs support solvent-saving SPME of bisphenols in food samples. Luminescent MOFs enable rapid fluorescence detection of trace bisphenols. MIP-modified COFs improve electrochemical sensing of bisphenol analogs.

title: Enhancing electrical and magnetic performance of carbon fiber polymer composites with Fe₃Si for lightweight, high-efficiency synchronous reluctance motor rotors
abstract: The demand for lightweight and energy-efficient electric motors in electric vehicles, aerospace, and industrial systems has driven the exploration of alternative rotor materials. This study introduces a novel Fe₃Si-enhanced carbon fiber-reinforced polymer (CFRP) composite rotor designed for high-speed synchronous reluctance motor (SynRM) applications. Soft magnetic Fe₃Si microparticles were uniformly integrated into the CFRP matrix using a hand lay-up method with dry particle deposition, resulting in enhanced magnetic permeability and reduced electrical conductivity while preserving structural integrity. The optimized composite rotor core achieved a weight and rotational inertia reduction of 38.12% compared to conventional electrical steel (ES) rotors core, with a reduced density of 4857.95 kg/m³. Furthermore, by strategically reducing the rotor magnetic pole arc angle from 145° to 130°, the lower intrinsic permeability of the composite was effectively compensated. Electromagnetic simulations revealed that the optimized Fe 3 Si-enhanced CFRP composite rotor achieves a peak efficiency of 94.0%, closely matching the benchmark ES rotor (95.4%), while suppressing eddy current and core heating due to the discontinuous conductive network of the polymer matrix. These results highlight the potential of Fe 3 Si-CFRP composites as lightweight, high-efficiency core materials for next-generation electric machinery.

title: Harnessing impedance matching and destructive interference: a modular asymmetric nanofibrous conductive network for tunable absorption-dominant EMI shielding
abstract: Abstract Addressing the challenge of achieving simultaneous high absorption and high electromagnetic interference shielding effectiveness (EMI SE), this work presents a modularly assembled alternative to Salisbury screens. The material is constructed on a modified electrospun TPU film with a designed three-layer architecture. The top layer is a CNTs-wrapped nanofiber porous network for impedance matching, the bottom is a silver-coated nanofiber network ensuring complete reflection, and a precisely tuned intermediate layer enhances destructive interference. This study systematically examines how the conductivity of the matching and bottom layers, along with interlayer thickness, govern overall EMI SE and absorption. The analysis reveals the optimal synergy between impedance matching and interference cancellation and clarifies the role of the conductive nanofiber network. The resulting composite, C5/T4/A3, achieves an EMI SE of 72.75 dB with only 0.04 wave reflection and a 3.40 GHz low-reflection bandwidth ( R < 0.1) covering 81% of the X-band. The simulated radar cross section value of the C5/T4/A3 simulated radar was the lowest within the wide θ range of -90° to -90°, and the peak decreases to -12.62 dBm 2 when θ = 0°. The replaceable bottom layer enables direct tuning of EMI SE by varying its conductivity, without changing the core mechanism. This work provides valuable guidance for designing absorption‑dominated, high‑performance EMI shielding materials.

title: Reconstruction-tunable upcycling of spent LiFePO4 cathodes for oxygen evolution electrocatalysis: from defect legacy to operating active interfaces
abstract: Spent lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathodes offer limited economic value through conventional metal recovery routes, but their Fe–P framework and cycling-induced structural heterogeneity make them promising precursors for oxygen evolution electrocatalysts. This review develops a reconstruction-centered framework that connects battery degradation with catalyst evolution under anodic polarization. Rather than treating inherited defects as intrinsic active sites, this review evaluates how cycling-induced defects, lattice disorder, phase boundaries, and vacancy chemistry regulate the susceptibility of reconstruction. Reported upcycling routes are classified according to precursor structural continuity into direct electrochemical activation, component- and interface-modulated reconstruction, and framework conversion coupled with secondary reconstruction. Despite their distinct precursor structures, many reported systems evolve toward Fe/Ni-based (oxy)hydroxide-rich operating interfaces, although their composition, coordination environment, and reconstruction pathway remain highly dependent on precursor chemistry and electrochemical conditions. Performance is compared beyond overpotential by considering feedstock origin, activation history, current density, cell voltage, temperature, and operational lifetime. Key unresolved challenges are further discussed, including defect–reconstruction relationships, reconstruction kinetics, substrate-derived contributions, feedstock variability, and phosphate stability during saline electrolysis. This review positions spent LFP as a reconstruction-tunable pre-catalyst platform and discusses mechanistic, device-level, and sustainability considerations for practical anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE).

title: Bioinspired composite fibrous membranes with phase-change radiative cooling for all-weather personal thermal management
abstract: Daytime radiative cooling offers a passive, energy-free pathway for personal thermal management, but nighttime overcooling remains a critical challenge. Inspired by the hierarchical structure of silkworm cocoons, we design a multifunctional composite fibrous membrane featuring a well-defined core-shell heterostructure via one-step coaxial electrospinning. A poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF-HFP) shell encapsulates a n-octadecane phase-change core, integrating radiative cooling with thermal energy storage in a single composite system. The PVDF-HFP shell provides strong Mie scattering and high mid-infrared emissivity via its micro-/nanofibrous structure and C–F vibrations, while the PCM core delivers thermal buffering through reversible latent-heat exchange during solid-liquid transition. A honeycomb-like corrugation on the membrane surface creates a micro-scale and concave-convex topography, boosting solar reflectance and thermal regulation. This composite design achieves excellent radiative cooling performance (solar reflectance \(\:{\stackrel{-}{R}}_{solar}\) =97.2%, infrared emissivity \(\:{\stackrel{-}{\epsilon\:}}_{IR}\) =94%), high latent heat storage/release capacity (∆ H c =122.6 J/g, ∆ H m =122.86 J/g), good thermal stability and thermal buffering capacity, and superior wearing comfort. Moreover, the core-shell interface effectively ensures leakage-free performance even after repeated thermal cycling, while the structured surface imparts hydrophobicity (water contact angle = 137.3°) and mechanical robustness (4.38 MPa). Outdoor tests further confirm the synergistic effect of daytime cooling (7.6 °C reduction vs. ambient) and nighttime overcooling suppression, validating efficient all-day thermal management. This work offers a composite materials design strategy for all-weather thermal regulation, with promising applications in energy-saving personal comfort and building thermal management.

title: Response of ZnO nanorod-modified multilayer aramid fabrics with varied thread densities to sequential ballistic impacts
abstract: This work addresses the critical challenge of enhancing ballistic resistance while preserving the flexibility of body armor via the fabrication of ZnO nanorod grown aramid fabrics. ZnO nanorods were grown in situ on plain-woven aramid fabrics with low (P8: 8 ends/cm), medium (P9: 9 ends/cm), and high (P11: 11 ends/cm) thread densities. We systematically explored the coupled effects of fabric density and nanomodification under sequential multi-angle ballistic impacts (6 shots at angles of 0°, + 30°, and − 45°). The results demonstrate that ZnO nanorods substantially increase inter-yarn friction as well as tensile and tear strengths, with only a minor impact on fabric flexibility (increase in bending length < 12%). Notably, the modified medium-density fabric (P9-Z-45L) achieved the optimal performance under six consecutive impacts on a single specimen: its average back face signature (BFS) decreased from 33.45 mm to 23.77 mm, with no penetration observed across all six shots. In comparison, the modified high-density fabric (P11-Z-37L) exhibited a limited BFS reduction of 13.88% and experienced complete penetration under oblique impacts with angle of -45°. Further analysis reveals that the nanorods promote energy dissipation through mechanical interlocking, enhanced yarn engagement, and constrained fabric deformation, which collectively improve energy absorption capacity. This study provides a density-dependent design strategy for flexible, high-performance body armor.

title: A wireless biofluid pH sensor based on a biomass-derived carbon/polyaniline hydrogel
abstract: Flexible sweat pH electrodes require sensing layers that combine a proton response with mechanical deformability. Here, we prepared a composite hydrogel sensing layer (CPN-AB + PVA) by in situ oxidative polymerization, combining boronic acid-functionalized polyaniline, corn-stalk-derived porous carbon and a polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) network. Interactions between the boronic acid-functionalized polymer and PVA connect the proton-responsive component with a stretchable network. The hydrogel exhibited an elongation at break of 285%. The resulting electrode achieved a sensitivity of 85.62 ± 0.79 mV pH − 1 in buffers from pH 2.00 to 8.00 and retained a linear potentiometric response under bending. Coupling the electrode with a Bluetooth readout module enabled continuous sweat pH recording during exercise. The composite sensing layer brings together mechanical deformability and high potentiometric sensitivity for flexible sweat pH measurement.

title: A two-stage statistical reconstruction method for characterization of anisotropic Cu–W composites from 2D cross-sections
abstract: This paper introduces a novel two-stage statistical reconstruction technique for generating realistic, anisotropic, three-dimensional Representative Volume Elements (RVEs) of multiphase, heterogeneous materials from perpendicular two-dimensional microscopy data. The proposed three-dimensional reconstruction method can generate 3D representations of multi-phase heterogeneous microstructures (including systems with more than three phases) featuring complex anisotropic patterns, while simultaneously accurately accounting for both phase clustering and agglomeration. Moreover, the present method can be employed for 3D reconstruction based on any microstructural statistical descriptor. The technique, employing Cellular Automata and Monte Carlo methods, accurately preserves critical microstructural features, including two-point correlation functions, phase distribution, morphology, and volume fractions, minimizing errors in the full two-point correlation function. This approach effectively bridges the gap between 2 and 3D analyses by enabling accurate meshing and high-resolution finite-element simulations (using tools such as Avizo, Ansa, and Abaqus) to predict anisotropic electrical and thermal conductivity. To ensure reliability, a detailed investigation of RVE size effects was carried out, with particular focus on anisotropic microstructures, verifying both numerical convergence and statistical representativeness within the finite element framework. The proposed workflow was experimentally validated using two copper–tungsten (Cu–W) composite samples, showing consistency between the 3D simulation results and measured electrical and thermal conductivity data. While AI-based reconstruction methods are powerful, they typically require large training datasets and intensive computation. In contrast, the technique presented here delivers high accuracy with minimal data input, making it especially suitable for applications where experimental data is limited or difficult to obtain.

title: Supramolecularly driven segregated graphene networks in polymer composites for electrothermal self-healing and damage sensing
abstract: Conventional thermally activated self-healing polymers often require external heating and lengthy recovery times for structural repair, as heat is transferred relatively inefficiently through convection. To overcome these limitations, Joule heating integrated through a percolated conductive filler network can be successfully employed. However, efficient electrothermal conversion requires the robust development of a highly conductive network within the polymer composite matrix. This study introduces a graphene/ureidopyrimidinone-functionalized poly(ε-caprolactone) (UBNP-G) composite that achieves rapid self-healing via electrical Joule heating. A segregated conductive network, formed through the interplay between the two-dimensional geometry of graphene and dynamic supramolecular interactions, exhibits exceptional electrical conductivity (10²–10⁴ times higher than that of one-dimensional UBNP–carbon nanotube composites at equivalent filler loadings). In contrast to one-dimensional fillers that remain randomly dispersed, graphene induces a phase-separated conductive network within the supramolecular polymer matrix. Molecular dynamics simulations support the distinct filler–polymer interactions responsible for the formation of the segregated network. Monitoring electrical resistance through the polymer composite provides a reliable measure of structural damage and recovery. Passing electrical current through the segregated network enables rapid self-healing within approximately 40 s at both room temperature and extremely low temperatures, without the need for external heat. These advancements present an effective strategy for designing multifunctional polymer composites for self-healing and structural health monitoring under diverse environmental conditions. During the review of the proof, we noticed that a critical statement regarding author contributions was omitted. Please add the following equal contribution note to the author information section or as a footnote on the first page: "Ohnyoung Hur, Yeong Jun Yu, and Ji-Hwan Ha contributed equally to this work."

title: Comparative study on the electrochemical corrosion behaviour of Al-Fe joints fabricated via compound casting, magnetic pulse welding, and diffusion bonding
abstract: In this study, the corrosion behaviour of an aluminium alloy AA6061/mild steel (MS) joint fabricated by solid-liquid (compound casting) and solid-state joining methods (magnetic pulse welding and diffusion bonding) was investigated through electrochemical corrosion in the presence of a 3.5% NaCl solution. In solid-liquid compound casting, applying a coating to MS before joining influenced corrosion behaviour. While Cu-coated MS provided good corrosion resistance, Ni-coated MS showed optimal integrated mechanical and corrosion characteristics. In Magnetic Pulse Welding (MPW), the 14.5 kV MPW joint showed the best corrosion resistance compared to the 14 kV sample, which suffered higher corrosion due to unbonded regions at the joint interface. Optimized welding energy and interface integrity are key to minimizing corrosion in high-impact solid-state welding processes. Corrosion rate during diffusion bonding depends on the process parameters and the interlayer’s effect at the interface. Pitting, IGC, and cracks in the intermetallic compound (IMC) are observed in the SEM-EDS analysis. Irrespective of technique, the interface’s corrosion behavior was found to be banking heavily on bonding parameters, IMC thickness and morphology, and defects in IMCs. Corrosion is mainly due to the anodic dissolution of the aluminium alloy due to a galvanic couple, and voids in the transition region accelerate the corrosion performance.

title: Wood-based functional nanomaterials for CO2 capture
abstract: With rising atmospheric CO 2 levels, amine-based solvents and porous solid adsorbents have advanced considerably, but still suffer from high energy costs, instability, and environmental issues. Wood, as a renewable material with hierarchical pores and tunable surface chemistry, has attracted growing interest for sustainable CO 2 capture. This review systematically covers recent progress in wood-based nanomaterials for CO 2 capture, encompassing diverse precursors such as cellulose, hemicellulose, lignin, delignified wood, bark, sawdust, black-liquor-derived products, and porous carbons. A precursor-based classification is introduced, and hardwoods are compared with softwoods to highlight how their anatomical and chemical traits affect pore structure and capture performance. Preparation strategies for porous carbons, aerogels, and membranes are discussed in relation to structure–performance trade-offs, alongside physical, chemical, and synergistic modifications. Applications in CO 2 capture, catalysis, life cycle analysis, and machine learning are also summarized. This review offers design principles for sustainable, high-performance wood-based CO 2 adsorbents and identifies future research directions.

title: Photo-switchable molecular solar thermal fabric composite for solar energy storage and self-powered motion sensing
abstract: Smart textiles integrating molecular solar thermal storage (MOST) are an emerging class of wearable systems, with prior work limited to microencapsulated azo-switches for thermoregulation and only scarce exploration of integrated energy harvesting and self-powered sensing, highlighting the need for system-level integration of multifunctional capabilities. Here, a hierarchically engineered woven Kevlar textile is reported that integrates MOST-based thermoregulation with triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) functionality. Azopyridine (APY) MOST nanocapsules are spin-coated onto Zn-Mo-Se nanoflake–grown fibers forming mechanically robust textile. Structural and spectroscopic analyses confirm conformal nanoflake growth and excellent microcapsule integrity over repeated photocharging–discharging cycles. Reversible photoswitching is achieved (98.8% Z under 365 nm and 97.8% E under 520 nm), enabling reversible solar energy storage and on-demand heat release. The Zn-Mo-Se –MOST textile exhibits a high energy density (457 J g⁻¹), storage lifetime (98 h) a maximum heat-release temperature of 56.4 °C, and a 77.1% increase in tensile strength compared to bare WKF. Notably, the color evolution of the fabric directly reflects the stored thermal energy state, enabling real-time visual monitoring. Simultaneously, the textile functions as a high-output TENG (1.7 mW cm⁻²), enabling stable, self-powered detection of human-motion and tactile gestures. This work advances MOST textiles toward scalable, adaptive, and self-powered wearable platforms. A hierarchically engineered molecular solar thermal textile (woven Kevlar) composite integrates photo-switchable solar energy storage and triboelectric performance within a single platform. Reversible photoswitching enables high energy density, long storage lifetime, and on-demand heat release, while the same textile delivers self-powered human-motion sensing with high power density. This work establishes a multifunctional route toward autonomous wearable energy and sensing systems.

title: 3D printed iron oxide nanozyme contact lenses for oxidative stress reduction
abstract: 3D printing facilitates a wide range of novel possibilities for ocular healthcare. 3D printed therapeutic contact lenses can be useful for the prevention and treatment of ocular diseases like dry eye syndrome and bacterial keratitis. This work explores 3D printed iron oxide nanozyme incorporated contact lenses for oxidative stress reduction. Iron oxide nanoparticles can behave as nanozymes, providing oxidative stress reduction in the eye. Here, 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate (HEMA) and polyethylene glycol diacrylate (PEGDA) lenses are 3D printed, and iron oxide nanoparticles are then incorporated within these lenses through in situ precipitation. Nanoparticle formation and catalytic activity are studied for different HEMA: PEGDA ratios. The nanoparticle concentration was found to increase with HEMA ratio in the hydrogel. Nanozyme lenses displayed catalytic activity in the presence of hydrogen peroxide, demonstrating their oxidative stress reduction capabilities. While HEMA: PEGDA 100:0 ratio had the largest nanoparticle concentration, HEMA: PEGDA 75:25 was the best for catalytic activity and methylene blue removal. All the nanozyme lenses exhibited good cell viability with human dermal fibroblasts. In addition to cytocompatibility, HEMA: PEGDA 75:25 lenses displayed significant cytokine suppression, establishing them as a promising candidate for safe, multifunctional contact lens applications. Hydrogels with iron oxide nanoparticles also respond to external magnetic fields due to the superparamagnetic property of these nanoparticles. The results indicate that there is great potential for the production of iron oxide nanozyme contact lenses with tunable properties through 3D printing.

title: Multifunctional composite materials for integrated CO2 adsorption and catalytic transformation
abstract: Global climate change necessitates innovative approaches to carbon capture and utilization (CCU). Traditional sequential processes, involving separate capture and conversion stages, often suffer from high energy penalties and operational complexities. This review highlights the emerging paradigm of multifunctional materials that simultaneously perform CO 2 adsorption and its catalytic transformation into valuable products. Recent advances in designing such integrated hybrid systems are comprehensively summarized, with emphasis placed on composite architectures based on metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), covalent organic frameworks (COFs), layered double frameworks (LDFs), and MXenes. The review elucidates fundamental mechanisms where adsorption sites facilitate CO 2 pre-concentration and activation for subsequent catalytic reactions on integrated active centers. Key performance metrics, such as adsorption capacity, catalytic efficiency, product selectivity, and long-term stability under integrated conditions, are critically evaluated. Finally, current challenges and future research directions for developing highly efficient and scalable multifunctional adsorbents-catalysts are discussed, aiming to accelerate the development of sustainable CCU technologies.

title: Exceptional compressive performance in additively manufactured CoCrNi-based hybrid metamaterials enabled by sequential yielding and gradual strain release
abstract: Metamaterials are promising candidates for advanced structural applications owing to their exceptional strength-to-weight ratio, energy absorption, and fatigue performance. Realizing these potentials simultaneously requires moving beyond monothetic topology design and developing novel strategies to integrate contradictory mechanical behaviors within components. Here, the design freedom of additive manufacturing is leveraged to break this long-standing performance paradigm via embedding precipitation-hardened inner fillings into a ductile matrix, constructing hybrid metamaterials with high resistance to compressive damage and cyclic fatigue. This design enables a novel strain-dependent, sequential yielding deformation in which soft outer layers dissipate energy during initial compression, followed by progressive engagement of the inner fillings. An observed dual-plateau compressive response synergistically enhances plateau stress and energy absorption. Under cyclic loading, thermally stable cellular structures containing coherent γ′ precipitates alter damage progression and suppress cyclic ratcheting. The acquisition of four-stage fatigue behavior, featuring a stage of gradual strain release, extends fatigue life by over 100%. The synergetic effect of nanoscale precipitation, microscale substructures, and a macroscopic compositional gradient enables strain redistribution and redirects damage to high-tolerance regions. This design presents a novel methodology for fabricating hybrid metamaterials with incompatible mechanical properties, yielding fatigue-resistant structures with enhanced compressive energy absorption for aerospace, automotive, and biomedical applications.

title: Hierarchical chiral core–shell FM/CNF@P–CoFe composite fibers for broadband microwave absorption via guide–capture–dissipate
abstract: Balancing impedance matching with sufficient electromagnetic attenuation remains a central challenge in the development of broadband microwave absorbers. Here, hierarchical chiral core–shell FM/CNF@P–CoFe composite fibers were constructed by textile twisting of a ferromagnetic microwire (FM) and a carbon nanotube fiber (CNF) into a heterogeneous double-helical core, followed by deposition of a porous nanofibrous shell containing Co/CoFe 2 O 4 . Systematic variation of the Co/CoFe 2 O 4 loading revealed a loading-dependent balance between impedance matching and internal attenuation. Although FM/CNF@P–CoFe–18 retains a relatively high attenuation constant over part of the investigated frequency range, FM/CNF@P–CoFe–12 provides the most favorable balance between impedance matching and internal attenuation. Based on the effective electromagnetic parameters measured for the aligned assemblies, FM/CNF@P–CoFe–12 yields a calculated minimum reflection loss ( RL min ) of − 42 dB and an effective absorption bandwidth ( EAB ) of 9.6 GHz at a matching thickness of 1.75 mm. Comparative full-wave simulations further indicate topology-dependent redistribution of the internal electromagnetic field associated with the heterogeneous double-helical core. These results support a “Guide–Capture–Dissipate” (GCD) framework describing the roles of impedance regulation, field redistribution, and electromagnetic dissipation. Homogenized equivalent-layer simulations further predict a radar cross-section (RCS) reduction of at least 14.6 dB m 2 at 12 GHz over incidence angles up to 60°. Overall, broadband absorption in this hierarchical composite fiber system arises from a favorable balance between impedance matching and internal attenuation, with the double-helical topology mediating internal electromagnetic-field redistribution.
